articles.title: After Jaspal Rana’s sudden demise, Paris Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker forging new bonds with Serbian coach
articles.summary: More sports News: BHOPAL: After adjusting the lighting at the MP State Shooting Academy final hall, two young electricians asked Manu Bhaker if she needed anything else.
articles.body: BHOPAL: After adjusting the lighting at the MP State Shooting Academy final hall, two young electricians asked Manu Bhaker if she needed anything else. “Nahin,” the shooting star politely replied. The electricians were still waiting. Distracted, Manu suddenly realized it hadn’t hit home, and gave them a thumbs up with a smile.Job well done, the men left the range content.With that stardom and popularity that surrounds her, the Paris Olympics double medallist may have realised at that moment, that a lot rides on her validation.Nearly a decade ago, in 2017, Manu, already a teenage star, was known to getting things done her way. Calling it stubbornness would perhaps be much; insistence on her plans, especially those concerning her sport, was her weapon. It was also the reason for her success.She has a different weapon now -- flexibility. While a certain doggedness suited her teenage self, flexibility is becoming of a mature Manu.Other than being a good judge of situations, Manu is also mastering the art of changing according to its demands.After the sudden passing away of her coach, Jaspal Rana, two months back, Manu has adapted herself with Serbian coach Jelena Arunovic.The Indian star, attending the Asian Games camp here, has been spending over eight hours at the ranges. She reaches the range at 7.30 am and is the last to leave with Jelena late afternoon. In between, some intense training happens.“Her openness to new methodologies has definitely made the transition to a slightly different way of working easier,” Jelena told TOI.“I think her flexibility comes first from the fact that she is never completely satisfied with her current level. She is always looking for what can still be improved, either to achieve a better result or to make her performance more stable. That is actually a trait of top athletes,” she added.The shooter is forging a bond with her new coach, spends hours with her at the ranges, and follows the unconventional ways of training that the Serbian brings. The 24-year-old does all this, without fuss or frown.“I think flexibility at this level does not mean accepting every change immediately. It means being able to understand why something is being changed, test it seriously, and then see whether it can actually help your performance,” Jelena, who had coached her sister Zorana to a gold in Paris, said.It isn’t just about training under a new coach. It is also about training with different ideas and different philosophies. With less than two years left for the 2028 LA Games, the star of 2024 looks in no mood for complacency. She rather looks hungry for more and is doing everything to repeat her performance.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Week 12 College Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Pickups: Richard Young, Calvin Russell III among top targets for playoffs
articles.summary: With the college fantasy football playoffs underway in Week 12, here are Eric Froton's top waiver wire targets.
articles.body:
The college fantasy football playoffs are officially here, and there is no margin for error with your lineup decisions this weekend. If you have any deficiencies with your skill position groups, there are several quality starting options still available in the majority of Yahoo leagues.

Note: Week 12 waivers will process overnight Tuesday due to Week 11 being extended to accommodate college football games that were moved to Sunday.

The fifth-year phenom has been positively electric in Big 12 play, throwing for 280+ yards in eight straight games with multiple touchdown passes in seven of them. He has scored 20+ points in every game except for a Week 9 loss to Texas Tech, when he threw for 417 yards and still managed to produce a respectable 18.2 points. It's fair to say that Fifita has one of the most stable floors of any quarterback in the P4. His 24 touchdowns passes rank fifth among all P4 signal callers and Fifita's 253.3 total points (25.3 PPG) ranks ninth. He faces a reeling Kansas State team that has lost four straight and ranks 112th in yards per successful dropback allowed (15.8). Fifita is an excellent starting option if you're looking for a boost at QB for the playoffs.

What more can you say about the breakout campaign Gio Lopez has had this season? He returned after missing last week's tuneup against FCS Merrimack to utterly destroy ACC foe SMU 49-7 with Lopez recording 27.4 points in the blowout. With Lopez having scored 27+ points in six of his nine appearances, and playing Georgia Tech's 110th-ranked defense that allows 20.5% of its completions to gain 20+ yards, he is a top waiver priority in the 71% of leagues he is still available.

Since throwing two interceptions and getting pulled against UCLA, Raiola has gone five straight games without throwing a pick while completing 67% of his throws in that span. He was on point this week in a 31-7 beating of Michigan, throwing for 341 yards with four touchdowns for 28.9 points. Raiola is a credible QB2/3 streaming option against Michigan State this week if your QB1 is compromised or has a bad matchup.

An Alabama transfer this past offseason, Young was sparsely used in the early going, receiving 16 carries through the first seven games. However, that all changed on Halloween, when Young exploded out of nowhere for 24 carries, 120 yards, two touchdowns and 24.0 points in a 27-24 win over Kansas State. He was once again the catalyst for CU's offense this weekend, churning out 21 carries for 99 yards and two touchdowns in a shocking 42-32 upset of Big 12 contender Houston. He has a prime-time matchup against a Cincinnati defense that ranks 123rd in rushing success rate allowed and gives up 5.4 YPC. We also just watched ISU RB Aiden Flora put up a ridiculous 46.9 fantasy points against them on Saturday. It's wheels up for Young, who is firmly in play as an RB2 or flex starter this week.

Wisconsin OC Jeff Grimes went with Dupree as his starter this week. He had 18 touches and got the opportunity to cash in two short-yardage touchdowns for 19.8 points. Abu Sama had been the starter all season, but he didn't receive a carry until the second quarter and only saw three touches on the day. Dupree has been more dynamic than Sama and boasts higher marks in broken tackle rate, yards after contact and rushes of 10+ yards. Dupree should be a strong flex play against Purdue's porous run defense that allows 178 yards per game on the ground (110th) and ranks 134th nationally in explosive play rate allowed.

Carson Hansen, Penn State (35% rostered)

Hansen started the season a little slowly and didn't score over 12 points until PSU's Halloween showdown with Purdue. Hansen has emerged as a legitimate starting fantasy option since then, having scored 17+ points with 341 rushing yards over his last three games. It's important to note that he left Saturday's 42-14 destruction of Minnesota early after tweaking his ankle, but by that time he had already racked up a season-high 126 rushing yards and the game was well in hand. PSU HC Matt Campbell expressed optimism about Hansen's availability for their mouth-watering Week 12 matchup against Rutgers' poor defense that allows 192 rushing yards and 32.3 points per game. Just make sure to stay vigilant about checking his health status before tossing him in your lineup.

Phillips has amassed 251 yards on 44 carries over the last two games, taking over for the injured Kamari Moulton. He should receive another 20+ carry load and is a rock-solid starter this week against Illinois.

Calvin Russell III, Syracuse (1% rostered)

The crown jewel of Syracuse's freshman class, Russell was unable to play until Oct. 3, catching two passes for 14 yards in his first two appearances as he got acclimated to the collegiate game. It's safe to say he settled into his starting role, accruing 54 targets, 397 yards and three touchdowns over his last five games. He officially broke out as a fantasy star this week against NC State, catching an eye-popping 17-of-18 targets for 137 yards and a touchdown, adding 24 rushing yards for good measure as Russell erupted for 30.6 fantasy points, which led all P4 wideouts in Week 11. He has a very favorable matchup against a Boston College D that allows 2.34 points per drive (100th) and ranks 108th in marginal explosiveness, and should be a major waiver priority for WR-needy teams, as Russell may have just stolen the WR1 role from Umari Hatcher.

Don't confuse Aidan with his younger brother, Isaiah, who is also a standout receiver for Arizona. Regardless of which Mizell you'd like to reference, both of them have evolved into legitimate WR1s at their respective schools. Aidan had been used primarily as a deep-ball specialist early in the season after transferring in from Florida, where both his parents were also student athletes. That all changed two weeks ago against Minnesota with Mizell catching not one, but two 75-yard touchdown passes in a 34-20 win. Clearly he caught the attention of the coaching staff, as Mizell recorded career highs in targets (10), receptions (six) and receiving yards (176) in the rain-soaked 22-14 victory over Illinois. The Bruins play Michigan in Ann Arbor this weekend, but if Mizell can pop for 26.6 points in the first UCLA home game since 2012 to be rained upon, I'm confident he can handle the November Michigan weather after the Wolverines just got carved up by Oregon 31-7.

Jeremiah McClellan, Oregon (6% rostered)

Welcome back, Jeremiah! The rising receiver was an important part of Oregon's late-season playoff push last season, and had been electric in Oregon's opening week 34-27 win over Boise State, reeling in six-of-nine passes for 150 yards, a touchdown and 24.0 points. Unfortunately, McClellan was injured after just one reception in Oregon's Week 2 loss to Oklahoma State, and hadn't suited up for several weeks until he checked in with a reception against Ohio State in Week 10. Now healthy, McClellan diced-up Michigan, catching four-of-five passes for 105 yards and a touchdown for 18.9 points this Saturday. Keep in mind, McClellan looked like the WR2 opposite Dakorien Moore at the beginning of the year and is a better bet to produce fantasy-relevant stats then Evan Stewart down the stretch. McClellan is well worth a speculative add against Michigan State this weekend.

Giovanni Richardson, Arizona (5% rostered)

While Richardson was written up in my Week 11 waiver wire column, he is still only 5% rostered despite catching 23-of-37 targets for 355 yards and 53.4 points over his last three games. He and QB Noah Fifita have shown a strong connection since Richardson returned from injury three weeks ago, and are a superb QB/WR combo against Kansas State this weekend.

Luke Dehnicke, Northwestern (2% rostered)

A preseason sleeper who received praise in fall camp, Dehnicke started strong out of the gate and looked like an every-week starter after he secured all seven of his targets for 140 yards against a stout Indiana defense in Week 4. Unfortunately, he got hurt in the process and wasn't able to play again until Oct. 31. Since his return, Dehnicke has reasserted himself as a factor in the Northwestern passing game, catching 13 passes for 183 yards and a touchdown over his last three games, with this week's 17.3-point detonation against Ohio State being the second-highest score among all P4 tight ends this week. He is an excellent starting option this weekend against a Minnesota defense that has given up 76 points over the last two weeks and ranks 131st in completions of 20+ yards allowed.

The lead returning receiver for the Blue Devils, Hasley has come on strong lately, having recorded 12.5+ points in two of the last three games. He should be a focal point of the offense and receive another 8-10 targets against a reeling Clemson team that just got embarrassed 20-6 by lowly 3-7 Georgia Tech.

articles.title: Week 11 Fantasy Football Early Waiver Wire Pickups: Xavier Hutchinson, Antonio Williams among top options
articles.summary: Who's looking good off the waiver wire? We examine some potential adds for fantasy football to start Week 11.
articles.body:
We're approaching Week 11 of the 2026 fantasy football season and bye-pocalypse is nearly upon us. We have six teams on bye in Week 11 — the Packers, Rams, Seahawks, Patriots, Browns and Falcons. With so many teams off, you're likely going to have at least a hole or two in your lineup for a key matchup. We're here to help with some potential adds off the waiver wire.

Xavier Hutchinson, WR, Texans (2% rostered on Yahoo)

The Houston passing game has really been clicking in two contests since the bye. Last week, we saw C.J. Stroud and Co. tear up the Chargers. In Week 10, the party continued (albeit in a stunning loss to the Browns) with Stroud tossing three TDs, one to Hutchinson, who now has a score in three straight games. He was second behind Nico Collins with four catches on seven targets for 58 yards and the TD, his third straight game reaching double-digit fantasy points.

There are going to be weeks in which the Texans spread it around, particularly once Marvin Harrison Jr. is back from injury. But the run game is non-existent for Houston, which should mean the team leans on the pass even more down the stretch. Hutchinson is playing the majority of snaps and is developing chemistry with Stroud. The wideout isn't a bad pickup if you need a spot start at WR or FLEX with Houston set to face the lowly Colts in Week 11.

Antonio Williams, WR, Commanders (26% rostered)

Looking back to that TNF matchup between Washington and New York, Williams was a key contributor with two catches, one going for 31 yards and a TD. If we're chasing opportunity, Williams led Commanders WRs in snaps with 59 (86%) in the win. He finished with a 2-42-1 line for 11.2 fantasy points, and while we'd like to see Jayden Daniels give Williams more looks, that could be on the horizon. We hear the sentiment that rookies tend to improve in the second half and it's looking like Williams will be a priority in the passing game with Terry McLaurin out for the season.

Similar to Hutch, Williams is a decent WR or FLEX option with a potentially great game script in Week 11 against the Bengals. Williams has long-term value as well with solid matchups against the Cardinals, Titans and Texans after that.

We're all wide receivers in this edition, baby! Our third wideout recommendation is a player who will be coming off a bye in Denver's Bryant. He would have been a trendy pickup for Week 10 had the Broncos not been off, following a useful 4-56-1 line against the Panthers. Bryant has missed most of the 2026 season but when healthy, he's posted decent numbers with at least 6.2 fantasy points in four of five contests.

That isn't a huge figure but it's a decent floor for a player who may go overlooked on the wire this week. We also know that Jaylen Waddle sustained a concussion in Week 9. He should have ample time to get back for Week 11, but in the event Waddle is out, Bryant would get a nice boost. He's another target if you need a WR or FLEX option.

articles.title: Ryan Wedding's 'billion-dollar drug empire': Feared LA gangster accused of leaking FBI secrets to Olympic fugitive
articles.summary: Roberto Gomez, a fugitive Los Angeles gang member known as “Fat Boy,” has been charged with allegedly helping former Canadian Olympic snowboarder Ryan
articles.body: Roberto Gomez, a fugitive Los Angeles gang member known as “Fat Boy,” has been charged with allegedly helping former Canadian Olympic snowboarder Ryan Wedding run a billion-dollar drug trafficking operation. A six-count federal indictment accuses Gomez, 51, of supplying drugs and passing sensitive law enforcement information to Wedding, including details about planned arrests, drug seizures and search warrants. Prosecutors say the information helped Wedding avoid capture while the network moved cocaine, methamphetamine and fentanyl across borders. Gomez remains a fugitive in Mexico. The charges are allegations, and he is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.Roberto Gomez allegedly passed police intelligence to Ryan WeddingThe indictment says Gomez had links to people connected to the Sinaloa Cartel and Cártel de Jalisco Nueva Generación (CJNG), as well as contacts who could access confidential information held by Mexican and U.S. law enforcement agencies.The Justice Department said: “While in Mexico, Gomez met and communicated with leaders of foreign terrorist organizations, including the Sinaloa Cartel and Cártel de Jalisco Nueva Generación (CJNG), and cultivated relationships with individuals who had access to law-enforcement sensitive information from Mexican and U.S. agencies”.It added: “Gomez obtained that information related to law enforcement operations, including arrests, drug seizures, warrant executions, and the filing of criminal charges and provided this information to his co-conspirators, including Wedding.”The alleged assistance ran from October 2024 to January 2026, according to the indictment.Gomez is also accused of acting as a drug supplier for several criminal groups between 2016 and 2026. Prosecutors say he arranged for cocaine, methamphetamine and fentanyl to be moved into Mexico through Central America by air and sea before being transported overland to the United States and Canada.The indictment also says Gomez tried to arrange a sale of about 1,000 pounds of methamphetamine to Wedding. The deal was allegedly worth around $550,000, to be paid in cryptocurrency.Ryan Wedding faces 17 federal charges after January arrestWedding represented Canada in snowboard competition at the 2002 Winter Olympics in Salt Lake City. U.S. authorities later accused him of leading a major international drug operation and ordering several murders. He was placed on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list before he was arrested in Mexico on January 23, 2026, and brought to the United States.Wedding, 45, has pleaded not guilty to 17 felony charges across two federal cases. The charges include drug trafficking and murder-related offences. He remains in U.S. custody.Gomez had been living in Mexico after leaving Los Angeles County in 2000, when he was charged with two counts of second-degree robbery. A federal grand jury in Los Angeles indicted him again in 2018 on drug trafficking and money laundering charges. He is still wanted in both cases.If convicted on all counts in the new case, Gomez faces a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years in federal prison and a maximum sentence of life.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Fantasy Football: Joe Burrow stamps MVP case in Week 10 while Christian McCaffrey turns back the clock
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Chris Allen goes over the top storylines coming out of Week 10's Sunday action.
articles.body:
I start collecting notes on the games soon after kickoff. And I'm not just jotting down what happened, but an angle on the action. For instance, while the Jacksonville "Trevor Washingtons" were playing well in the first half, the running game was stuck in neutral. However, we (I, mostly) forget how quickly things can change. Sunday wasn't just about early-game narratives flipping, but even perspectives from the previous week getting challenged.

Anyway, let's go through some of the top storylines from Week 10 and what they could mean for fantasy.

Last Wednesday, I made the rest-of-season bold call that Joe Burrow could challenge Josh Allen for the QB1 spot in fantasy. I'll admit my track record on bold calls hasn't been great this season (I've gotten close!). But like my other hot takes, this one was rooted in some reality. Burrow just needed to maintain his pace of play. And if this is the only call I get right, I'm OK with it.

Pittsburgh, with two weeks to prepare, came into the game allowing the third-fewest passing TDs. They were fourth in sack percentage. Their secondary was limiting opposing offenses to the ninth-lowest passing success rate. Since the Bengals were coming back from Madrid, the Steelers had all of the advantages a defense would need outside of playing on their home turf.

And still, No. 9 put up an MVP performance.

Passing Success Rate: 62.2%, 1st (of any QB to play against PIT)

Pittsburgh tried blitzing him throughout the first half and twice to start the third quarter. Burrow was a perfect 11-for-11 for 143 yards. Six of those throws turned into first downs. The Steelers' only sack was on a similar pass-rush concept in the first quarter. Afterward, Burrow was under duress just five more times. This time, it was Ja'Marr Chase who took the spotlight , hoarding 14 of Burrow attempts for an absurd 54.8% share of the air yards. However, it wasn't just about the WRs making big plays. Instead of just pushing the ball downfield, the ancillary options in the short area of the field helped set up the intermediate daggers to keep the offense on schedule.

Chase Brown had his best day of the season on Sunday night. Not only was he back up to a 50% rushing success rate on early downs (first time in a month), but he continued to make plays as a receiver. Even if you take away his two short receiving TDs, half of his catches resulted in a first down. Along with Dohnte Meyers and Drew Sample chipping in, Burrow showed they can sequence dink-and-dunk catches with the Chase or Tee Higgins explosive waiting to catch any defense lacking.

Washington has its own mini-bye after playing on TNF, so it has a few days' head start before the Bengals travel down to Landover in Week 11. But it just gave up almost 300 yards to J.J. McCarthy. And with the way Cincinnati's offense has been putting up points, the MVP chants for Burrow will only intensify.

It was just seven days ago when I was heaping praise on Jordan Love and the Packers' passing attack. The whole operation, minus the occasional drop from Matthew Golden, looked easy. DC Brian Flores reminded Green Bay that defenses can be more complicated from time to time.

The Vikings defense reset Love's single-game, career-high sack total from five to eight. He now has three games in the season with double-digit hits from the opposing defense. Minnesota owns two of them. However, the problem wasn't just Love's health being at risk. And it wasn't that he fell below 250 passing yards for the first time since early October, either. Flores had Love playing a different style of football.

Passing aDOT: 8.6 (Week 10), 10.0 (Last Six Games)

Middle-of-the-Field Throw Rate: 61.5%, 46.6%

Coming into Week 10, Love had the fourth-most yards on throws to the perimeter. He tacked on just 45 against the Vikings. He was fifth in EPA per dropback on throws of 15+ air yards. One, after averaging 9.6 attempts per game of similar depths in Weeks 1-9, Love just threw four similar passes in the divisional rematch. And two, the majority of the completions didn't come until the second half. The one positive was that Love kept the same trust in his WRs as he had in weeks past (complimentary). But, as I mentioned for Golden, his play remained unchanged (derogatory).

To be clear, I'm not knocking Golden for the drop. Love came right back to him on the next drive for the Packers' first explosive play of the game. However, in a game where the margins were already thin, adding to his league-high drop total only helps the people who roster him. Because yet again, Golden (31.0% target rate, 22.0% air yard share) and Christian Watson (17.2%, 22.0%) dominated the opportunities. And not much changed for Tucker Kraft. The Packers used two or more TEs on 61.1% of their offensive plays (season-high), but Kraft's utilization (78.4% route rate, 13.8% target share) didn't dip. Playing the Vikings was just a complete 180-degree shift from their previous opponents. Luckily, they've got the bye week to recalibrate before facing the Rams in Week 12.

I'll answer my own question here. I'd say James Cook III is properly rated. Actually, we answered this question back in August. Players don't just randomly wind up with a single-digit ADP. That's especially the case when their QB turns into a vulture at the goal line. So, it shouldn't be too surprising to see Dalvin's younger brother put on a show.

Honestly, it's better seeing Cook back in this condition compared to last week . And sticking with Buffalo's bout with Minnesota, Cook is the lesser-discussed reason for the Bills coming out on top. Jahmyr Gibbs is the only other RB to face the Vikings this season and churn out more than 100 yards on the ground. And those gains didn't just help the people rostering Cook. In the second half, with a stronger lean on the run (PROE down to -10.3%), his early down runs set up Allen with more manageable passing situations (average 7.2 yards to the sticks). That's where his complementary play to Allen's becomes critical to Buffalo's success. The numbers bear out the same story.

Rushing Success Rate: 47.1%, 10th (out of 18 qualifiers – min. 50% rushing share)

Adj. Yards After Contact per Att.: 3.95, 7th

On a per-touch basis, few have done it better than Cook. Of the 18 RBs with more than half of their team's carries, Cook has seen the highest rate of eight or more defenders in the box (54.5%). And yet, he's one of the five rushers in that same category with a positive EPA per tote. Plus, with Allen leading his offense, even fewer have access to the same number of opportunities. Only Javonte Williams has played more snaps from inside the five-yard line. Of course, Cooks' problem is that less than half of those plays have turned into actual touches (15 of 32).

Cook has been what we wanted Chase Brown to be. Cook can grind out short yards or break off an explosive play like any of his peers. But being a caddy to one of the league's best QBs has its weekly drawbacks. You'll get outings where Allen will have the only rushing scores. But with someone like Cook on your roster, you'll take the highs and lows.

Christian McCaffrey, Still Good At Football

If you played against Christian McCaffrey today, just close your league app.

Hey, sometimes these things happen. In hindsight, with the 49ers going up against Dallas' defense, the chance for a knockout performance was always possible. But seeing it in real time was one of the best performances of 2026.

If there was any credit to give to Dallas' defense, they were at least able to keep McCaffrey bottled up as a rusher. Through two quarters, his eight attempts resulted in just 21 yards on a 12.5% success rate. The same was the case for Kaelon Black. His lone carry picked up four yards. As a rushing unit, the 49ers had just one first down from non-Brock Purdy runners.

I know this section is about McCaffrey, but Black plowing through Caleb Downs for the TD deserved its own highlight. Regardless, rushing success rates for both RBs were up to 40+% to close out the game. But McCaffrey's real damage was done as a receiver.

I realize per-route metrics need more than 17 routes to stabilize. But the video-game results are too gaudy to let slide. Purdy buying time with his legs and pulling multiple defenders forward is the type of offensive harmony you don't see too often. Every target to McCaffrey added 4.2 EPA. Half of his catches turned into explosives.

Unfortunately, the 49ers go from an easier defensive matchup to the Vikings and Seahawks in back-to-back weeks. But with McCaffrey this effective as a receiver, his floor should be worth a start every week.

I can see both sides of the "letting a QB sit behind a veteran" debate. Not everybody's ready to play at the NFL level. Besides, Las Vegas' coaching overhaul was in its infancy, and Kirk Cousins was the ideal operator for HC Klint Kubiak's under-center, play-action offense. But the Raiders planned to start Fernando Mendoza soon anyway. I would've opted for his debut to come against a different opponent, and the results were about as I expected.

Vegas' opening script went as well as Kubiak designed it. The offense marched right down the field, with Mendoza capping off the drive with the same draw play that helped him earn a title . But a few things to consider before adding him to your list of viable streamers. First, the drive started on Seattle's side of the field after Drew Lock fumbled . Second, of the 11-play series, Mendoza threw the ball three times. No pass went farther than four air yards. Most importantly, Brock Bowers was on the field for just two snaps on that drive. And without Mendoza's "WR1," much of the play-calling tendencies that kept the offense on schedule for Cousins went out the window.

The Raiders ran 11-personnel (three-receiver sets) on 65.7% of Mendoza's dropbacks. For reference, their previous high was 58.1% back in Week 2. But here's where playing against Seattle's defense in your first start amplifies the issue. Ten of Mendoza's 19 pressures came in 2.5 seconds or less. And with just one pass-catcher above the 50th percentile in creating separation , Mendoza's average time to throw continued to tick up. Seattle pressured him on 48.7% of his dropbacks, and he did complete over half of his throws under duress. But the result was just two first downs.

We don't know the severity of Bowers' injury yet. And both of the Raiders' opponents before their bye have top-five marks in pressure rate. As a result, it might be toward the end of the season before we see the best of Mendoza and the Raiders.

articles.title: Former Washington Huskies Forward Off to Historic Start in G-League
articles.summary: Hannes Steinbach has performed consistently since being assigned to the Greensboro Swarm by the Charlotte Hornets.
articles.body:
The Washington Huskies men's basketball team had to replace nine spots on the roster going into this season.

One of the players the Huskies were tasked with replacing included the team's top scorers and rebounder in the 2025-26 season, forward Hannes Steinbach.

Steinbach was a one-and-done player with Washington after being recruited out of Wurzburg, Germany. He made enough of an impression to get on many NBA team's boards going into the 2026 NBA Draft.

Steinbach was ultimately selected with the final lottery pick (14th overall) by the Charlotte Hornets .

The German forward looked to the billing of being a lottery pick in the Summer League and the preseason, but struggled to break through the rotation of the Hornets when the regular season began.

Through the first 13 games of the season, Charlotte is 4-9 and on the outside of the playoff picture (and the play-in) and occupies the 11th-seed in the Eastern Conference.

Steinbach has played in five of the Hornets' 13 games. In his limited action (12.6 minutes per game), he's averaged 2.8 points per game on 43.8% shooting from the floor and is yet to attempt a 3-pointer. He's also brought in 4.2 rebounds per game.

As a result of his limited action with Charlotte, the team has opted to move him up-and-down between the NBA roster and its G-League affiliate, the Greensboro Swarm.

With the Swarm, Steinbach has shown the form that made him a lottery pick in the first place.

According to a post on "X" from Greenboro's official account, Steinbach is the first player in G-League history to score more than 75 points and bring in more than 50 rebounds in his first three games. His total rebounds (56) were second in that stretch in G-League history behind Eric Mika and his total offensive rebounds (24) in that stretch were tied for the most in that stretch, tying Vincent Hunter and Justin Williams.

In his time in the G-League, Steinbach has averaged 25.3 points on 60% shooting (60% from 3-point range) and has pulled in 18.7 rebounds while while dishing 1.7 assists and blocking 2.7 shots per contest.

In his lone college season in the Pacific Northwest, Steinbach averaged 18.5 points across 30 games (all starts) on a 57.7% clip from the floor (34% from beyond the arc). He also registered 11.8 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.2 blocks per game.

Steinbach finished his one-and-done college career with third-team All-Big Ten honors, led the nation in rebounds per game and co-led the nation in double-doubles with then- Duke Blue Devils forward Cam Boozer, who was selected third overall in the '26 draft by the Memphis Grizzlies .

articles.title: Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Makes Statement on George Pickens Future Despite ‘Disappointment’
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys got a great performance out of George Pickens on Sunday in what was otherwise a "disappointing" loss. The post Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Makes...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys' loss to the 49ers on Sunday featured so many distressing defensive play that it would be easy to overlook the fact that quarterback Dak Prescott poured just about all he had into the game, repeatedly pulling the team back from what appeared to be desperate deficits to give Dallas a chance late in the game. And it would be easy to overlook the fact that, without question, receiver George Pickens had his best game of the season, the kind of game many had been waiting for here in his second go-round with the Cowboys. Not only did Pickens catch 11 passes (he did have at least two drops, however) but he tallied 145 yards and three touchdowns, repeatedly going at and beating the 49ers' Demmodore Lenoir.

The Cowboys lost, 46-40, and fell to 4-6 on the season in doing so. But the breakout game for Pickens will at least re-ignite the question of just how good this offense can be when it is clicking–and when both Lamb and Pickens (who had a hamstring injury and missed Week 9) are healthy and working the field.

Jerry Jones Sees 'Positive' of George Pickens

After the game, as so often happens, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones held court with reporters and was asked about the way Pickens played–and whether seeing the offense look so productive affects how Jones might consider paying Pickens in free agency next winter.

Said Jones when asked if he thinks the Cowboys can build around Pickens: "I sure do. George is a positive, a real positive. They do some outstanding things with George and Dak, CeeDee. Those should be big assets for us and tonight, I have to say they kept us where we at least thought if some good things happened at the end, we might have a chance. So, yeah, I think they're a big part of it."

In the end, though, Jones was left disappointed by the Cowboys' performance, mostly because the 49ers did just what Dallas expected them to do but the defense was powerless to stop it.

Jones continued: "We had the right assessment of what kind of team they are, the record speaks for itself, they're an outstanding team. We didn't play as well in the second half as we did in the first half. … The things we thought they were going to do, they beat us with it. The quarterback was outstanding. They made plays. They made a lot of yards. And we're aware of that.

articles.title: Oilers’ McDavid Ties One of Gretzky’s Many Records
articles.summary: Edmonton Oilers superstar Connor McDavid has been chasing down Wayne Gretzky throughout his entire career, but now he’s tied one of his records once again.He...
articles.body:
Edmonton Oilers superstar Connor McDavid has been chasing down Wayne Gretzky throughout his entire career, but now he's tied one of his records once again.

Heading into Sunday's game, Gretzky was the sole player in NHL history to record 40 assists in just 22 games. Even then, he was only able to do so once in his career. He did it in 23 games on two occasions, but he was never able to do it in 22 games again following the 1984-85 season. Then, as the Edmonton Oilers faced the Philadelphia Flyers on Sunday night, McDavid became the second to do so, as first reported by Sportsnet.

When Leon Draisaitl scored his 19th goal of the season just 8:08 into the first period, McDavid picked up the primary assist on the play, his 40th of the season in the Oilers' 22nd game. He then picked up his 41st assist of the season later in the period with another primary helper, this time scored by Zach Hyman.

It's hard to argue against Connor McDavid being a future Hockey Hall of Famer, even if he were to retire tomorrow, he'd earn an induction very quickly. With that being said, he's entering a level of production that hasn't been seen yet in the 21st century. He's currently pacing to become just the second player in league history to surpass 200 points in a single season. The only player to do so is the aforementioned Gretzky, who did so four times. Mario Lemieux nearly did it during the 1988-89 season, but fell short by just a single point.

Even if McDavid only makes it to 160 points, which would require an average of just under two points-per-game, he'd become the first player besides Lemieux and Gretzky to do so. McDavid is already just one of just six players in NHL history to record more than 150 points, earning a career-high of 153 points during the 2022-23 season.

This season, McDavid has now registered 52 points in his first 22 games which leads the NHL by quite a large margin. His teammate, Leon Draisaitl, currently sits second in the league with 40 points through his first 22 games. The NHL hasn't seen a talent like Connor McDavid in a long time, and who knows when another will come around.

When Wayne Gretzky recorded 40 assists in 22 games during the 1984-85 season, the Oilers went on to win the Stanley Cup. The Oilers have been close to doing so during McDavid's time in the organization, making their way to back-to-back Stanley Cup Finals appearances in 2024 and 2025, but were never able to win the seven-game series as they fell to the Florida Panthers on both occasions.

Now, the Oilers are undoubtedly hoping that history can repeat itself. If McDavid is able to produce at this high of a level, it's hard to imagine any team being able to contain him for the entirety of a seven-game series. McDavid put a lot of effort into convincing the Oilers to bring in head coach Mike Babcock, and now he's showing exactly why he wanted a coach who could motivate and push him even further.

articles.title: Cowboys QB Dak Prescott admits trying to trick his mind amid 49ers fan takeover
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott admitted he tried to convince himself that the sea of red at AT&T Stadium represented his high school rather than vis...
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott admitted he tried to convince himself that the sea of red at AT&T Stadium represented his high school rather than visiting San Francisco 49ers supporters. The unusual admission followed Dallas' 46-40 defeat, which added to the Cowboys' struggles under Brian Schottenheimer.

Prescott anticipated a significant visiting crowd before Sunday's matchup. However, seeing so many opposing fans inside his home stadium still made an impression.

The Cowboys quarterback acknowledged the overwhelming 49ers presence during his postgame comments.

"Tricked myself, told myself the red was for my high school," Prescott said.

"Unfortunately, their fans were more present than ours."

Prescott explained that he expected San Francisco supporters to travel in large numbers. He also emphasized that the atmosphere remained enjoyable despite the unusual balance of support.

The quarterback confirmed Dallas never needed to use a silent count, even with the considerable noise generated by visiting fans.

On the field, Prescott delivered five touchdown passes, but his impressive offensive performance wasn't enough to secure a victory. San Francisco quarterback Brock Purdy countered with 389 passing yards and three touchdowns.

The defeat highlighted another frustrating afternoon for Dallas, which struggled to contain the 49ers' explosive offense. San Francisco also forced two turnovers, including a late fumble recovery that sealed the result.

Prescott has previously defended Schottenheimer amid criticism, but the latest loss adds pressure on the Cowboys to turn their season around.

For Dallas, the disappointing result came with an uncomfortable reminder of its home-field challenges. Prescott's lighthearted attempt to reinterpret the crowd colors couldn't hide how strongly San Francisco supporters represented their team.

articles.title: “Want To Apologize”: Iowa State HC Bill Fennelly Releases Statement After Facing Suspension For “Inappropriate Contact With a Student-Athlete”
articles.summary: The relationship between a coach and a player comes with a responsibility that extends beyond basketball. Iowa State has addressed that responsibility after...
articles.body:
The relationship between a coach and a player comes with a responsibility that extends beyond basketball. Iowa State has addressed that responsibility after an incident involving women's basketball head coach Bill Fennelly, who is facing a one-game suspension after an incident involving inappropriate contact with a student-athlete during the Cyclones' game against UIC. Now, following that decision, Fennelly has responded.

"I want to apologize to the student-athlete and her family, her teammates and all of Cyclone Nation for allowing my emotions to get the best of me during our game," Fennelly said in a release on the team's website.

"I fully recognize that there are no situations where it is appropriate to make contact with a student-athlete in that way. I accept responsibility and will serve the suspension and I will do better moving forward."

The incident occurred with about two minutes left in the game and Iowa State up by four. During a timeout huddle, Fennelly yelled at Sienna Harvey, then put his hand on her head and nudged her. Following the game, Iowa State athletic director Jared Benko directly addressed the situation.

"We cannot tolerate inappropriate contact between a coach or staff member and a student-athlete in practice or in competition, whether intentional or not," Benko said in the same press release.

"We have high expectations of all of our coaches, staff and student-athletes and we will not shy away from holding accountable those who fail to meet those expectations. I have met with Coach Fennelly and he has apologized to the student-athlete involved and regrets his actions."

According to the release, Bill Fennelly will serve the suspension when Iowa State takes on UNI on November 18. Associate head coach Caroline McCombs will take over the acting head coach responsibilities.

The timing of the situation and his statement adds a difficult layer to an already significant season for Bill Fennelly. In October, the longtime Iowa State coach announced that he is planning to retire at the end of the 2026-27 season, which will bring an end to a tenure that began in 1995. He is currently in his 32nd season with the Cyclones.

Before joining Iowa State, he spent seven seasons at Toledo, compiling a 166-53 record and leading them to three NCAA Tournament appearances.

"While I still love coaching and am working as hard as ever, I understand that this job has an expiration date," he said about retirement. "After talking with my family, I have made the decision that the 2026-27 season will be my last. Announcing my intention now is what is best for everyone in our program and provides the new athletics director clarity on my future and allows them to make plans for the program moving forward."

Bill Fennelly has accepted responsibility and said he will do better moving forward, and his absence against Northern Iowa will be his consequence for the incident.

articles.title: OTD (16/11/1996): Sunderland Lose Their Spurs At The Lane
articles.summary: A difficult afternoon at White Hart Lane saw Sunderland lose 2-0 and finish with ten men. But as Bob Murray prepared to invest millions, could better times b...
articles.body:
Peter Reid's side got off to a good start in our first season in the top flight since the big rebrand. The FA Carling Premiership was the place to be and, after a surprise promotion that followed a fight against relegation to the third tier, Sunderland were part of it.

After a victory over Coventry City at Roker Park via a Steve Agnew goal, we'd managed to win three of our first seven league games. We did, however, pay a big price to take three points from Ron Atkinson's side that day, because Niall Quinn was lost to a long-term knee injury that would see him miss most of the season.

A few weeks later, we lost our new signing between the sticks when Tony Coton suffered multiple breaks in his leg in a 3-0 defeat at The Dell. With our two big signings out long-term, things looked a little less rosy.

By the time we travelled to White Hart Lane to take on Gerry Francis' Spurs side on this day in 1996, we'd picked up just four points from the previous fifteen on offer and had begun to slide down the table.

Ahead of the game, Reid had a crisis in defence. With Richard Ord suspended and Lee Howey out with an ankle ligament problem, the assumption was that Kevin Ball would move from midfield to slot in alongside Andy Melville. In the end, it was Martin Scott who filled the void in central defence, and Dariusz Kubicki came in at left-back.

Spurs took the initiative in the early stages and, after forcing a good early save from Lionel Perez, it came as no surprise when they took the lead after twelve minutes. Andy Sinton beat Gareth Hall and David Kelly down their left before beating Perez with a low drive that went in off the post.

Less than ten minutes later, Spurs had the ball in the back of the net again, only to see it ruled out for offside, and Sunderland were hanging on. Teddy Sheringham missed a sitter not long after that, but despite their dominance, Ball could have levelled against the run of play but failed to hit the target from six yards out when it looked easier to score.

Reid's side were fortunate to go in at the break just one goal down, and fifteen minutes into the second half we made our lives more difficult when we were reduced to ten men. Paul Stewart was harshly sent off a few weeks earlier at Highbury, but this one was deserved after a two-footed challenge on Colin Calderwood.

With ten minutes left on the clock, the game looked to be over when Kelly tripped David Howells just inside the area and Mike Reed pointed to the spot. Sheringham stepped up but gave Sunderland hope of taking something out of the game when he struck the outside of the post.

Two minutes later, however, Sheringham made no mistake. Darren Anderton crossed from the right and the former Millwall and Nottingham Forest striker doubled the home side's lead.

[Sinton 13', Sheringham 82' – Stewart sent off 57']

Back in the days when it was a thing to announce how much managers had to spend in the market, Bob Murray revealed on this day in 1996 that his manager had £7m available to strengthen the team. It was also reported that this could rise to £12m following the planned flotation a month later.

Sunderland were to be the eighth club to float on the stock exchange, and the hope was that £10-15m would be raised in doing so, although part of the money was to be used to pay off the debts incurred during the building of the new stadium, with Murray stating:

We are taking a £7m turnover business to £20m within two years. That's what we are hoping to do. The stadium is the catalyst for everything.

With the new money burning a hole in Reid's pocket, the first name on the list to spend it on was Israeli international Ronen Harazi. On this day in 1996, Harazi was due to begin a week-long trial at Sunderland and was hoping to follow Eyal Berkovic, who made a similar move to Southampton weeks earlier.

The striker had been recommended by former Sunderland player and Darlington manager David Hodgson, and his club, Beitar Jerusalem, are believed to have wanted £400,000 for the 26-year-old.

Harazi had scored 18 goals in 36 international appearances after replacing Spurs' forward Ronny Rosenthal in the national side. David Pleat at Sheffield Wednesday had also been keeping tabs on the player, as he was pencilled in for a reserve team fixture in midweek, but Harazi seemed confident ahead of his week on Wearside:

I've only got until Friday to prove myself, but I am confident I will make it. There's no problem with my fitness. I was injured a month ago, but I came on as a substitute in Cyprus this week and I am in good shape.

articles.title: Luka Doncic Sends A Message To Lakers After Suns’ Fourth-Quarter Rally
articles.summary: Luka Doncic had 37 points through three quarters and figured his work was done for the afternoon. Instead, he had to check back in to help the Los Angeles La...
articles.body:
Luka Doncic had 37 points through three quarters and figured his work was done for the afternoon. Instead, he had to check back in to help the Los Angeles Lakers finish off the Phoenix Suns. The Lakers won 131-123 on Sunday for their eighth straight victory, but Doncic used his postgame interview to tell his team what it needs to do better.

"I wasn't planning on playing in the fourth quarter; we need to get better at that. I know we played badly, we finished badly, but we need to improve in that area. When we manage to get ahead, we have to hold on to the lead, and we have to work on that."

Phoenix scored 43 points in the fourth quarter, matching Doncic's total for the entire game. A lead that reached 31 in the third was down to five with just over a minute to play. By then, Doncic was back on the floor, and the Lakers still needed one more big shot.

Luka Doncic returns as the Lakers' lead shrinks

The Lakers were up 101-70 with 1:47 to go in the third. They still had a 24-point cushion when the fourth began. Phoenix kept chipping away, and Lakers coach JJ Redick took a timeout with roughly five minutes left and the margin down to single digits.

The Suns won the quarter 43-27. Doncic pointed to Phoenix's increased aggression and said the Lakers got sloppy coming out for the fourth. He also took hold of the coaching whiteboard to address teammates during the game, according to Bleacher Report.

Quentin Grimes gave Los Angeles breathing room in the final minute. With the Lakers ahead 126-121, he banked in a three to push the margin back to eight. Doncic added two free throws to close out the win. Grimes finished with 22 points, and Doncic paired his 43 with nine assists, per the box score.

Lakers lean on Doncic with Austin Reaves out

The Lakers played without Austin Reaves , who bruised his left heel in Milwaukee last week. Reaves entered Sunday averaging 24.7 points and 4.7 assists, leaving Los Angeles without one of its primary scorers and playmakers.

Doncic put up 20 points in the first quarter alone. He made three shots from beyond the arc and went 7-for-8 from the line in those opening 12 minutes. Late in the third, he drew MVP chants in Phoenix after converting a three-point play.

Phoenix was the last stop on a trip that took the Lakers through Detroit, Atlanta, and Milwaukee. Los Angeles had three days off after the Milwaukee game and finished the trip with a 12-2 record.

Redick had credited the team's offensive organization and disruptive defense during the winning streak while pointing to ball security and defensive rotations as areas that still needed work , as reported by the Los Angeles Times. He also said Reaves was improving and that his availability would come down to how much pain he could tolerate.

Los Angeles returns home Tuesday to face the Charlotte Hornets at Crypto.com Arena. The Lakers will have a chance to make it nine straight, with Doncic asking for a cleaner finish the next time they pull away.

articles.title: Trevor Lawrence breaks down what gives him confidence amid Jaguars’ winning streak
articles.summary: Trevor Lawrence has remained the barometer for the Jacksonville Jaguars, leading the team to its third straight win after disposing of the Tennessee Titans,...
articles.body:
Trevor Lawrence has remained the barometer for the Jacksonville Jaguars , leading the team to its third straight win after disposing of the Tennessee Titans , 40-23, at Nissan Stadium on Sunday.

Lawrence went 25-of-35 for 352 yards and three touchdowns. He also had four carries for 27 yards. The Jaguars notched their sixth win in seven games and improved to 7-2 to extend their lead in the AFC South. The Titans, meanwhile, fell to 1-8, including 0-5 at home.

FOX Sports' Ben Arthur pointed out Lawrence's efficiency this season , tallying 21 passing touchdowns and just five interceptions. He entered the week leading the league in touchdown rate at 8.0% and yards per attempt at 8.6.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

In the video posted by Arthur, the 27-year-old quarterback acknowledged his strong campaign, while also giving credit to his teammates.

"It starts with the confidence with what you're doing from the schemes standpoint. Just having the confidence. I know what I'm seeing. I've seen these plays a lot. I've seen the coverages. I feel like I'm processing really well right now, and that's a huge part of it. But then it all comes back to our guys, our players, the guys making plays. Just having that trust," said Lawrence.

"You can't really win by yourself, and the guys in front are protecting well."

Lawrence had a rocky start to his career after being the Jaguars drafted him with the No. 1 pick in 2021. But he has found his footing in recent years, making Jacksonville a strong contender .

Against the Titans, he became the eighth-youngest player in league history to reach 20,000 passing yards.

The Jaguars reached 30 points for the fourth straight week, tying the team record for the longest such stretch. They first did it in 2017.

They will visit the New York Giants in Week 11.

articles.title: Why Nikola Jokic is Still an NBA MVP Candidate This Season
articles.summary: Jokic got off to a slow start by his own standards, but his recent play and Denver's record keep him firmly in the MVP race.
articles.body:
A 116-108 win over the Pelicans on Saturday gave the Denver Nuggets a 7-4 record, and center Nikola Jokic was once again the reason why, finishing with 26 points, eight rebounds, 10 assists and three steals.

He made 9 of his 14 shots and all seven of his free throws in New Orleans, and the three-time MVP has been putting together nights that clean more often lately.

Jokic had a rough first two weeks of the season, with his shot not falling the way it usually does, and some people started to wonder if he was slipping.

Head coach David Adelman never bought that idea, and after a home loss to Portland on Monday, Nov. 2, he said the shots that Jokic almost never misses were coming.

He pushed the point even further in comments quoted in a column on Jokic's slow start .

"This is a six-game sample size of one of the most efficient offensive basketball players that's ever lived. I'll die on that sword."

Adelman has looked right since then, as Jokic has scored at least 25 points in each of his last three games through Saturday while making 30 of his 51 shots over that stretch.

After the win in Memphis, he talked about how playing with aggression and decisiveness was the key for the whole team.

Through Saturday's game in New Orleans, Jokic is averaging 23.7 points, 10.5 rebounds and 9.1 assists while shooting 51.0% from the field.

Those numbers sit below the 27.7 points, 12.9 rebounds and 10.7 assists he put up last season, when he finished second in MVP voting, but no other player in the league is averaging at least 20 points, 10 rebounds and nine assists.

His one real weak spot has been the three-point line, where he is shooting just 25.0%, and I expect that number to climb with time.

He also has three triple-doubles in 11 games and Denver won every one of them, including a 32-point night against Toronto when he said he let the game come to him instead of forcing anything.

MVP voters care about the standings, and that is where Jokic still has work to do.

Denver is seventh in the Western Conference through Saturday's games, three games behind San Antonio and the Lakers, who are both 11-2.

The Nuggets did win four of their last five games heading into this week, though, and guard Jamal Murray has helped carry the load by averaging 25.9 points per game through Saturday, which is a big reason the two are still one of the best duos in the league .

I believe Jokic belongs in the MVP conversation right now, because his slow start looks more like a short dip than a real decline.

His case will only get stronger if Denver keeps stacking wins and climbs into the top four in the West, and the Nuggets get a chance to build on this stretch at Ball Arena with Phoenix coming in on Monday, Nov. 16, and Boston on Wednesday, Nov. 18.

articles.title: ‘They Got Smashed’: Mike Tomlin Breaks Down Steelers’ Embarrassing Loss to Bengals
articles.summary: Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin did not hold back after the Steelers’ embarrassing 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati […]
articles.body:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin did not hold back after the Steelers' embarrassing 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday night. Both teams came into the game at 6-2, but the Bengals outclassed the Steelers in every facet.

"It was breakdowns in so many areas. I just think the first thing you've got to acknowledge is they got smashed," Tomlin said on NBC's postgame show. "They got smashed on defense, they got smashed on offense. They didn't get enough done in any of the phases for the storyline to take hold. There's something to be learned from it, but only if, and when, you acknowledge what happened. They ran into a buzzsaw."

Mike Tomlin on how bad the Steelers played: "They got smashed" Tomlin also dropped a we and said: "There's certainly some disappointment from a fans perspective" pic.twitter.com/eMkjG1o5K6 — Austin Bechtold (@AustinRBechtold) November 16, 2026

Mike Tomlin on how bad the Steelers played: "They got smashed" Tomlin also dropped a we and said: "There's certainly some disappointment from a fans perspective" pic.twitter.com/eMkjG1o5K6

Austin Bechtold (@AustinRBechtold) November 16, 2026

Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow tied a significant NFL record against the Steelers . Burrow tied Peyton Manning (5) for the most consecutive 4+ total touchdown games in a single season. Manning set the record in 2004.

In the first half, Burrow completed 26 of 34 passes (76.5%) for 302 yards with three touchdowns, no interceptions, and a passer rating of 132.2.

In the third quarter, Burrow captured his fourth touchdown of the night, completing a 4-yard pass to Chase Brown to extend the Bengals' lead to 30-3.

The Steelers' defense had turned heads this season, allowing only 16 points in their last two wins. The defense had no answer for Burrow and company, however.

"We didn't get enough four-man rush," Tomlin said, accidentally saying "we" when talking about his former club. "But they didn't get them in enough one-dimensional passing circumstances. The Steelers didn't possess the ball enough. They didn't convert enough third downs, particularly early on. When you get a solid lead, then you're not beholden to situations, so those circumstances that we talked about never really developed."

articles.title: Pat Freiermuth muscles in for tough touchdown
articles.summary: Pat Freiermuth scored a late 27-yard touchdown as part of a 2-35-1 line against the Bengals in Week 10.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers TE Pat Freiermuth had two catches (on three targets) for 35 yards and a touchdown versus the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 10.

Why It Matters: Freiermuth had a great individual effort to score on a 27-yard pass from Aaron Rodgers, giving anyone that plugged him into their lineups a boost on an otherwise dreary night for Pittsburgh's offense. For the veteran tight end, however, it marked the fourth straight game (and seventh in eight outings) that he has finished with less than 40 yards receiving. His five touchdowns do give him a puncher's chance at value, but Freiermuth is no more than fringe TE2.

articles.title: 'I should have never ever bought': Faf du Plessis reveals why Virat Kohli is the most expensive relationship of his life
articles.summary: Faf du Plessis revealed how Virat Kohli backed him unconditionally during his three-year stint as RCB captain from 2022 to 2024, despite the pressure of succ...
articles.body:
NEW DELHI: Faf du Plessis may have found an unwavering ally in Virat Kohli during his stint as Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) captain, but the friendship came with an unexpectedly expensive side effect: a newfound obsession with luxury watches. The former South Africa captain revealed that Kohli introduced him to the world of expensive timepieces, persuading him to buy watches he would never have considered otherwise. "So I've said this to him, and I've said this publicly: the most expensive relationship of my life has been him. Because he's made me buy watches that I should have never, ever, ever bought," du Plessis said in a conversation with ESPNcricinfo. He admitted that Kohli's influence had transformed him into a watch enthusiast, albeit one whose spending habits had become difficult to justify. "Three years later, I've become the biggest watch guy. And now everyone is saying to me, how do you spend that much money on a watch?" he said.

Kohli had du Plessis' back during RCB captaincy

The friendship between the two developed during du Plessis' three-year stint as RCB captain from 2022 to 2024. Taking over the leadership from Kohli was never going to be straightforward, given the Indian batter's immense popularity and his deep connection with the franchise's supporters. Du Plessis recalled feeling accepted by Kohli almost immediately after stepping into the role. "There was always respect, but in an instant I felt accepted to step into the shoes," he said. However, the pressure of succeeding Kohli was never far away. Du Plessis pointed out that even a single defeat could trigger demands from RCB supporters for the former captain to return to the leadership role. "Let me tell you as a captain, if you lose two games, not even, if you lose one game for RCB, the whole of Bangalore and the whole of India want Virat Kohli to captain," he said. "And it's not because they don't like you or me. They just want Virat Kohli to captain. So anything that doesn't happen that's a win comes down to: but Virat Kohli must be captain." Du Plessis understood the expectations that came with leading one of the most popular franchises in Indian cricket. What made the challenge easier, however, was the support he received from Kohli, who remained an important part of the dressing room despite relinquishing the captaincy. "Imagine if I didn't have that support, how I would have felt in those three years. It would have been the hardest time to deal with that," he said.

The change in their respective roles also helped the two build a closer relationship. Du Plessis had previously been a captain while Kohli led India and RCB. With the South African now in charge and Kohli playing under him, their dynamic took on a different dimension. "At that stage, I was a player coming from captaining someone and then not captaining the team anymore. So I had this fresh perspective that at least I was on the same level with him, now that he's a player," du Plessis explained. He described Kohli's backing as unconditional and said their friendship came naturally, despite years of competing against each other on the cricket field. "I had his support, more than unconditional support, from day one. He just had my back all the time," he said. "I would say we had always played against each other, but instantly we felt like we had a very, very good friendship. There's no context here to it. There's no background. It was just, like, straight away." For du Plessis, Kohli's support proved invaluable during his time as RCB captain, helping him navigate the expectations that came with succeeding one of the franchise's most celebrated players. The friendship, it seems, has endured beyond their time together at RCB, even if Kohli has left him with a considerably more expensive taste in watches.

articles.title: Russia out of junior ice hockey worlds after Canada’s entry refusal
articles.summary: Norway back in the tournament after being bumped to make room for Russia after a Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling.
articles.body:
Russia will not compete at the World Junior Championship (WJC) following host Canada’s decision to bar Russian players , the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) has said.

The IIHF announcement on Sunday came after the Russian Ice Hockey Federation sought to have next month’s tournament either relocated or cancelled.

Canada took the position in response to a Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling late last month that reinstated Russia to international hockey.

Canada’s Secretary of State for Sport Adam van Koeverden said on Wednesday that Ottawa opposes Russian and Belarusian participation in international sport “as long as Russia continues its war of aggression against Ukraine with Belarus’s complicity”.

The minister for immigration, refugees and citizenship “will take measures to individually assess and prevent Russian and Belarusian athletes and officials from entering Canada to compete, regardless of whether they already hold valid visas”, van Koeverden said.

The tournament features top male players below the age of 20 and is being held in the province of Alberta beginning in late December.

“The IIHF confirms that due to the position and restrictions formally communicated by the Canadian Government, the Russian U20 national team is unable to participate in the World Junior Championship,” the IIHF said in a short statement on social media on Sunday.

“After carefully assessing the feasibility of alternative arrangements, the IIHF Council has determined that Canada will remain as host and the tournament will proceed from 26 December 2026 to 5 January 2027 in Edmonton and Red Deer.”

The CAS ruling overturned the IIHF’s ban, which was imposed after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

The IIHF was vociferous in its disagreement over CAS’s decision, and its statement followed announcements from Norway, Denmark, Sweden and the Czech Republic that ⁠⁠⁠⁠their national teams will refuse to play against Russia at next year’s men’s World Championships in Germany.

The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association said last weekend that it had been informed that it would be bumped from the tournament to make room for Russia. On Sunday, it said it would now be in the tournament.

“The Canadian government has taken a clear position, and many nations have also taken a stand in recent weeks,” German Ice Hockey Federation CEO Frank H Lutz said.

“We now need that same level of planning security for our home World Championship in May, for the teams, the fans and all our partners. We therefore call on the IIHF to provide clarification soon.”

articles.title: España conquista 16 medallas en el Europeo de kickboxing
articles.standfirst: Juan de Quintana se proclama campeón continental por segunda vez y la delegación española saca cuatro billetes para los European Games
articles.summary: Juan de Quintana se proclama campeón continental por segunda vez y la delegación española saca cuatro billetes para los European Games
articles.body: La selección española de kickboxing se colgó 16 medallas, un oro, cuatro platas y 11 bronces, en el campeonato de Europa WAKO de Skopje (Macedonia del Norte). Además, cuatro de sus integrantes lograron plaza para los European Games de Estambul 2027. Juan de Quintana volvió a subir a lo más alto del podio continental en Light Contact -89 kg. Conquistó su segundo título europeo, después del logrado en 2024, y amplió su palmarés en el que también figura el oro mundial de 2023. Su actuación en Skopje tuvo un segundo capítulo con la medalla de bronce en Kick Light, también en la categoría de -89 kg. El reparto de medallas dejó siete metales en tatami, con un oro (el citado de Juan de Quintana) y seis bronces, y nueve en ring, donde España consiguió cuatro platas y cinco bronces. En esta última disciplina subieron al segundo escalón del podio Salma Hablouji (K1 -48 kg), Jordi Velasco (K1 -60 kg), Jaime Lizana (Full Contact -67 kg) y Jordi Requejo (K1 -75 kg). El resto del medallero español se completó con los bronces de Eduardo Valdor, Manuel Pérez, Kevin Koffi y Carlos Lozano —por partida doble, en Light Contact y Kick Light— en tatami, mientras que Alexia Martínez, Ángela Talero, Izaro Blanco, Sofía Hamidi y Adrián Martínez lograron el tercer puesto en sus respectivas categorías de ring. La delegación española estuvo integrada por 27 deportistas —16 de ring, 10 de tatami y uno de formas—, además de cuatro árbitros y ocho entrenadores, con el presidente de la Federación Española de Kickboxing y Muaythai (FEKM), Jesús Eguía, al frente. España también brilló en la competición de Para and Inclusive Kickboxing. El equipo, formado por 14 deportistas, fue el más numeroso del campeonato y consiguió más de 14 medallas. Cuatro deportistas de ring aseguraron su presencia en los European Games de Estambul 2027: Jordi Requejo (K1 -75 kg), Izaro Blanco (K1 -60 kg), Adam Aguaer (K1 -63,5 kg) y Sheila Martínez (K1 -52 kg). Jesús Eguía, presidente de la Federación Española de Kickboxing Y Muaythai, expresó su satisfacción por los resultados y destacó el trabajo colectivo detrás de estos éxitos. "Volvemos de Skopje muy orgullosos. Dieciséis medallas en un Europeo con este nivel, y cuatro deportistas clasificados para los European Games de Estambul, son el reflejo del trabajo diario de nuestros deportistas, entrenadores, árbitros y clubes", señaló. Eguía también quiso recalcar la actuación de Juan de Quintana y del equipo de Para and Inclusive. "Quiero felicitar especialmente a Juan de Quintana por su segundo título europeo y al equipo de Para and Inclusive, que una vez más ha demostrado que en el kickboxing no hay barreras", afirmó además la presencia de Rafael Soriano, embajador de España en Macedonia del Norte, en la última jornada del campeonato. "Seguimos trabajando con la vista puesta en 2027", concluyó.
