articles.title: Predicting Final Members of Team USA and Team Mexico at WWE Survivor Series 2026
articles.summary: The classic Survivor Series tag team elimination match returning at WWE Survivor Series 2026 after a five-year absence gives fans good reason to rejoice.
articles.body:
The classic Survivor Series tag team elimination match returning at WWE Survivor Series 2026 after a five-year absence gives fans good reason to rejoice.

The bout was announced as Team USA vs. Team Mexico, with the two teams featuring stars from SmackDown, Raw and AAA. Even with nothing currently at stake, it should be a fun showcase for 10 top talents who might otherwise miss out on the November 28 card.

Immediately following Crown Jewel, it was determined that Cody Rhodes would lead Team USA while Rey Mysterio would serve as the captain for Team Mexico. It was then confirmed that CM Punk and Je'Von Evans would join Rhodes, with Penta and Rey Fenix being added to Mysterio's squad.

That leaves two spots open on each all-star team, and any number of names could realistically fill them. AAA has plenty of people available for Team Mexico to choose from, and there are enough directionless Superstars on the red and blue brands right now that Team USA has no shortage of intriguing options.

These are the most likely possibilities for the final members of Team USA and Team Mexico at Survivor Series.

Seth Rollins has been conspicuous by his absence on WWE TV since SummerSlam. Seeing as how he isn't currently dealing with a major injury, however, he should be back on Raw relatively soon.

Interestingly, there's no one obvious path for him upon his return. He wrapped up his rivalry with Roman Reigns and shouldn't be pursuing the World Heavyweight Championship again anytime soon, so he'll essentially be starting from scratch.

In that case, he would be a fine fit for Team USA, simply so he can be brought back into the mix on Monday nights with a bang and work alongside some of Raw and SmackDown's biggest and brightest stars.

There was a point in time when he and Cody Rhodes were allies, and it would be a surreal sight for him to join forces with Punk after how long they spent at odds with each other. Whoever eliminates him (or helps him get eliminated for that matter) could be his next rival coming out of the event.

It was at the Thanksgiving week classic that Rollins debuted as part of The Shield 14 years ago, so it'd be only appropriate for him to be a part of the show this year.

El Grande Americano has been the biggest breakout star in AAA over the last year, going from being a comedy character on Raw to being the most beloved babyface on the entire AAA roster.

He really started to hit his stride after besting Chad Gable's Americano in a Mask vs. Mask match back in May before finally winning the AAA Mega Championship in September. He's largely been kept exclusive to the AAA brand since then but came across like a total star when he popped up on Raw in Mexico soon after.

Of course, the man portraying Americano, Ludwig Kaiser, wasn't actually born and raised in Mexico, but it wouldn't be too shocking of WWE to put him on Team Mexico, anyway. He has a close relationship with the captain Rey Mysterio in AAA and most fans would just be happy to see him.

At the very least, it'd give AAA more exposure at Survivor Series since he remains the reigning Mega champ, and having him eliminate someone from Team USA would be a big boost to the brand.

No one else from AAA at the moment feels like a big enough deal to take up one of the spots on Team Mexico, though someone like La Parka or Mini Vikingo would have way more to gain from being afforded that opportunity than Americano, who is a made man at this point.

It would be silly for Trick Williams to not at least be considered for a spot on Team USA given he's the United States champion.

Additionally, he's a star on the rise and has had an incredible rookie year. He's held the star-spangled prize on and off since WrestleMania 42 and has racked up wins over the likes of Sami Zayn, Baron Corbin and Carmelo Hayes.

He has future world champion written all over him and thus it wouldn't be a stretch to see him challenging for a top title sometime in 2027. With that in mind, he should be a part of Team USA so he can benefit from teaming with massive stars in Cody Rhodes and CM Punk.

Williams is likely headed for a feud with Damian Priest, but he can join Team USA while also continuing to defend his title against all comers. He recently failed to dethrone Zayn for the Undisputed WWE Championship and isn't doing anything else of note at the moment.

Williams being among the sole survivors would be huge for him.

Dragon Lee is one of the most exciting wrestlers to watch in all of WWE. His booking has vastly improved from where it was a year ago, and he's now a regular on Raw and competing in meaningful matches.

Lee has come close to capturing the Intercontinental Championship on countless occasions this year but became the number one contender once again last Monday night. Regardless of when he gets his next shot at the strap, he can easily be added to Team Mexico at Survivor Series.

With Rey Mysterio leading the team, Lee is a logical choice given how frequently they've teamed up this year. He'd obviously excel alongside him and The Lucha Brothers, as all of their aerial offense would make for a blast of a bout.

It'd also be odd for every luchador on the main roster to be a part of it but not Lee, so one of the two vacancies really should go to him. It'd be another chance for him to showcase his skills as well as face a few people he's never squared off against before.

A strong showing at Survivor Series would go a long way in ultimately elevating him on the card and earning him an eventual run with singles gold.

Chad Gable is right up there with Dragon Lee as one of Raw's MVPs in 2026 thanks to his consistently strong performances in the ring. He's also enjoying the greatest success of his career to date.

He held the Intercontinental Championship for only three months but had a memorable run in that time, delivering weekly bangers with the midcard of the red brand and making that title feel like the most coveted prize on Raw.

He dropped the belt to Ethan Page earlier this year and subsequently fell short of becoming number one contender, so Gable is free to do virtually anything else going forward. Between that and Gable being a U.S. Olympian, it should be a no-brainer to get him on Team USA.

At the end of October, Gable went one-on-one with CM Punk for the first time ever and shockingly went over in clean fashion. Although it wasn't acknowledged on television, Punk can mention on Raw that he gained respect for Gable from that match before recruiting him to the team.

Gable being a part of this stacked bout would serve as a nice culmination to the story he's had with all of WWE's luchadors this year.

Dominik Mysterio was the very first one to attempt to throw his name into the hat as a member of either Team USA or Team Mexico. He was quickly denied by both Rey Mysterio and Cody Rhodes before being laid out.

Mysterio and Rhodes have had their fair share of issues with Dirty Dom in the past, so it made sense that they wouldn't allow him to join with such ease. That's also what makes him such a compelling candidate, specifically for Team Mexico.

Despite showing zero signs of slowing down, Rey could be headed for in-ring retirement as soon as next year, and if so, he and Dom should team up at least one last time, albeit reluctantly.

Dom might be among the most despised stars in WWE today, but his accolades alone would make him a valuable asset to the team.

He wrapped up a year-long run as AAA Mega champion two months ago, so he has a track record of being a draw for the AAA brand. He's been spinning his wheels ever since and forcing him to team with his father would ideally get something going for him.

There's a strong possibility that weeks of begging and pleading to get on the team could lead to Dom getting eliminated almost immediately, but it would be a story worth telling in the coming weeks and get him back in the spotlight where he belongs.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: CM Punk Addresses Retirement, Ric Flair Reacts to Cena-Charlotte Promo, WWE Rumors on Mr. Kennedy
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

CM Punk is aware of the speculation surrounding his retirement, but the 48-year-old made it clear that he doesn't have any plans to hang up his boots anytime soon.

After WWE's NXT live event in Detroit on Saturday, Punk put an end to the retirement rumors in his post-match speech.

"There's a lot of rumors out there that maybe because I'm 48, I'm wrapping s--t up. I'm here to tell you guys that I am not. Rumors are always rumors, and I don't like addressing certain things since it gives them life, but let's put that to bed right now," Punk said (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News).

The former WWE Champion went on to reveal how long he plans to stick around, much to the delight of the fans in attendance.

"Y'all are stuck with me for at least five more years, and I will go as hard as I am currently until the wheels fall off," he declared.

Punk's bold declarations echoed his sentiment from earlier this year, when he told Busted Open Radio that he would continue to perform as long as his health permits.

"Where that end is, nobody knows. I don't even know. It's not measured in the length of a contract. It's not measured in matches," Punk said ahead of SummerSlam. "To me, honestly, it's measured in health. It's how I look, and more importantly, how I feel. Right now, I've never felt better."

Punk remains one of the faces of the company, so WWE would surely welcome his presence for another five years.

Ric Flair Reacts to John Cena-Charlotte Flair Promo

John Cena's return to SmackDown this past Friday was highlighted by his heartwarming promo with Charlotte Flair, as he told her he hopes she breaks his all-time record of 17 World Championships.

WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair, whose record of 16 world titles was broken by Cena, posted a quick reaction to the promo, thanking the 49-year-old for his kind words to his daughter.

Cena was on hand to announce Charlotte Flair as the latest entry in the upcoming John Cena Classic. The 14-time World Champion emotionally explained how Cena has influenced her career, and he gave her some words of encouragement.

"You never had it easy, you made it look easy," Cena told her.

Flair will now try to add another accolade to her legendary resume as she turns her attention to the John Cena Classic.

After 17 years away from WWE, Mr. Kennedy, also known as Ken Anderson, is reportedly back with the company.

Steve Carrier of Ringside News reported that Anderson signed a WWE Legends deal, returning to the company for the first time since being fired in 2009.

Anderson made his WWE debut in 2005 and quickly became a fan favorite. He won the United States Championship a year after his arrival and captured the Money in the Bank briefcase at WrestleMania 23 in 2007. However, his WWE Championship run never materialized, as an injury forced him to lose his title opportunity to Edge. He was never able to regain his momentum and was released from the company following concerns over his in-ring safety.

After departing WWE, Anderson joined TNA and found success, winning the TNA World Heavyweight Championship twice.

WWE Legends deals are typically used to allow the company to use former wrestlers' likenesses in merchandise, video games and other projects. Anderson isn't expected to make a return to television, but this deal opens the door.

articles.title: Ranking Roman Reigns' 10 Greatest WWE Matches
articles.summary: Roman Reigns is currently in the midst of the greatest run of his WWE career, with excellent matches, worthy title defenses and a renewed emphasis on proving himself between the ropes.
articles.body:
Roman Reigns is currently in the midst of the greatest run of his WWE career, with excellent matches, worthy title defenses and a renewed emphasis on proving himself between the ropes.

That is saying something, considering the bangers he had already delivered before dethroning CM Punk for the World Heavyweight Championship at WrestleMania 42.

In celebration of all that he has accomplished between the ropes in 2026, relive The Tribal Chief's 10 greatest WWE matches, ranked according to match quality, with historical significance providing a tiebreaker as needed.

The Shield vs. Daniel Bryan, Kane and Ryback (TLC 2012)

Reigns made his WWE main-roster in-ring debut in a late contender for Match of the Year in 2012, teaming with Seth Rollins and Dean Ambrose to battle Daniel Bryan, Kane, and Ryback in a Tables, Ladders, and Chairs match.

The outstanding, high-impact contest was all the more impressive given its late addition to the TLC card. It replaced CM Punk's scheduled WWE Championship defense against Ryback after the champion underwent knee surgery.

It is a testament to the other matches on this list, including his most recent stretch of excellence, that Reigns' 2023 encounter with Sami Zayn just misses the top 10.

A molten-hot Montreal crowd desperately wanted to see its hometown hero dethrone The Tribal Chief in the culmination of their months-long storyline. Instead, Reigns weathered Zayn's challenge and benefited from Jimmy Uso's interference before using a steel chair and a Spear to retain.

A clean finish would have propelled this match onto the list—and probably close to the top five.

10. Edge and Daniel Bryan (WrestleMania 37)

In his first WrestleMania main event as The Tribal Chief, Reigns defended the Universal Championship against Daniel Bryan and Edge in a Triple Threat match that marked a major chapter in the Bloodline saga.

An action-packed main event featuring extraordinary near-falls, Edge's increasingly ruthless pursuit of victory, and one of Bryan's last great performances in a WWE ring, it culminated with interference from Jey Uso and Reigns stacking both opponents for the pinfall victory.

Often overlooked amid the upheaval of WWE's pandemic era, this excellent match set the stage for some of Reigns' finest work over the ensuing five years.

The main event of SummerSlam 2022, the latest installment in the seemingly never-ending rivalry between Reigns and Brock Lesnar, was a throwback to the chaos and destruction of the Attitude Era.

The Beast Incarnate made his entrance by driving a tractor to the ring, then launched himself from its front-end loader onto Reigns to kick off the match.

The Last Man Standing match featured big bumps, high-impact spots, and an attempted cash-in from Austin Theory, whom Lesnar stopped with an F-5. Even Paul Heyman took a bump, suffering an F-5 through the announce table.

With the ring tilted by Lesnar's tractor and both men physically battered, The Usos helped Reigns bury The Beast under the announce table and chairs to secure the ten-count.

After so many encounters between the two, a chaotic brawl reminiscent of a bygone era was the perfect conclusion to their rivalry.

Predicting Final Members of Team USA and Team Mexico 🔮

The first match on this list from Reigns' momentous 2026 run saw him defend the World Heavyweight Championship in Mexico City against No. 1 contender and overwhelming crowd favorite Penta.

The Tribal Chief busted his ass to make Penta look like a legitimate main event competitor on Raw and a potential future world champion. He bumped around the ring and took both a Mexican Destroyer and a springboard variation, with the latter producing one of the match's standout near-falls.

He ultimately recovered, caught Penta midflight with a Superman Punch, and finished him off with a Spear. Despite the defeat, the luchador emerged looking like a main event star, delivering a performance that could win over even his doubters.

Penta's momentum continued just under four weeks later, when he won Money in the Bank and secured another opportunity to become world champion.

7. CM Punk and Seth Rollins (WrestleMania 41)

While world titles are at the center of many matches on this list, the Night 1 main event of WrestleMania 41 was about good, old-fashioned hatred between three of WWE's biggest stars.

Reigns despised Seth Rollins, a rival who could shake his typically unshakable demeanor thanks to their complicated history dating back to The Shield.

His animosity toward CM Punk stretched back to comments The Best in the World made following his departure from WWE more than a decade earlier, while their competing loyalties to Paul Heyman added another layer of tension.

In Las Vegas, Reigns had the chance to take down both men and stand triumphant on WWE's grandest stage.

What he did not account for was betrayal by his Wise Man, the architect of so much of his success over the preceding years.

A match layered with storytelling and dramatic near-falls culminated in Paul Heyman betraying both Reigns and Punk to align himself with Rollins, laying the foundation for The Vision.

The defeat set the stage for another chapter in Reigns' rivalry with his former Shield teammate, one whose payoff would come more than a year later. Still, the WrestleMania 41 Saturday main event easily eclipsed everything else on that year's 'Mania card and strengthened Reigns' standing among the greatest big-match performers in WWE history.

6. Braun Strowman vs. Samoa Joe vs. Brock Lesnar (SummerSlam 2017)

Take four heavyweights, let them beat the life out of each other in a high-impact main event with Raw's top championship at stake, and the result is a match that would make Big E smile.

Still in his Big Dog guise, Reigns was positioned as WWE's leading babyface as he challenged Brock Lesnar for the Universal Championship in a Fatal 4-Way that also included Braun Strowman and Samoa Joe.

The monstrous Strowman ragdolled Lesnar early on, driving him through two announce tables and overturning a third onto him, forcing The Beast to be stretchered away. From there, Strowman, Reigns, and Joe tore the house down until Lesnar returned, defiant and hell-bent on retaining his title.

Despite a tremendous effort from Reigns, his last-gasp attempt at a Spear ended with him hoisted onto Lesnar's shoulders and driven to the mat with the match-winning F-5.

Like their SummerSlam encounter five years later, this felt like a throwback to a different era and showcased how much Reigns excelled when given the freedom to get creative in a chaotic brawl.

5. The Shield vs. The Wyatt Family (Elimination Chamber 2014)

The Shield's best match as a unit came at Elimination Chamber in 2014, when they squared off with The Wyatt Family in one of that year's most anticipated matches.

A straightforward six-man tag team match, it captivated fans for over 20 minutes before a finale that served to highlight the connection Reigns would have with the audience before WWE Creative botched it for years.

Late in the match, Reigns stood alone against Bray Wyatt, Luke Harper and Erick Rowan, and did not hesitate to take the fight to them. The Big Dog took punishment from his opponents, then ate a clothesline and a big boot.

But he kicked out at two, drawing a huge ovation from the fans as he fired up.

Feeding off the energy of the crowd, he mounted one more comeback before Harper sacrificed himself by taking a Spear, allowing Wyatt to finish Reigns with Sister Abigail for the win.

The defeat helped put Wyatt over ahead of his match with John Cena at WrestleMania 30 and foreshadowed The Shield's breakup just over three months later. For Reigns, his standout performance offered more evidence that he was going to be WWE's leading man sooner rather than later.

The I Quit Hell in a Cell match from 2020 is a masterclass of cinematic professional wrestling and a contest that does not get nearly enough credit for being as epic as it was.

Reigns and Jey Uso delivered a physical bout featuring some of WWE's greatest in-match character work in a decade. Through their trash talk, facial expressions, and body language, they told viewers at home everything they needed to know about two men fighting for their futures. It was a phenomenal matchup from WWE's pandemic era.

Late in the roughly 30-minute contest, Reigns threatened to crush Jey with the steel steps, escalating the brutality against the cousin who had challenged his authority as Tribal Chief.

Jimmy Uso intervened and appeared to get through to The Head of the Table, only for Reigns to trap him in a guillotine choke. Desperate to save his brother, Jey uttered the words "I quit," losing the match and submitting to Reigns' authority.

Often overshadowed by what followed, this remains a defining chapter in the Bloodline saga and deserves an immediate rewatch.

More than a decade of history hung over Reigns and Rollins as they entered the ring for the Night 2 main event of SummerSlam 2026.

From their days in The Shield to Rollins' betrayal and his role in helping Cody Rhodes end The Tribal Chief's tyrannical title reign, the two had plenty to draw on when the bell rang in Minneapolis.

Packed with callbacks to their shared history, the match captivated fans as Reigns tried to overcome the rival who could get inside his head better than anyone else. Rollins, meanwhile, sought to leave SummerSlam with the World Heavyweight Championship for the second consecutive year.

With nods to their biggest encounters and tributes to their Shield teammate, Dean Ambrose, Reigns and Rollins tore the house down in a brilliant one-on-one match. The OTC delivered three Spears to finally put Rollins down, bringing a fitting sense of closure to their shared story.

Their post-match fist bump, with Rollins' Shield mask resting between them as a symbolic stand-in for Ambrose, added an emotional final touch and conveyed how much their shared history meant to both men.

By the time WrestleMania 42 arrived, Reigns had spent years associated with Bloodline interference and elaborate storyline twists. This offered a different test: Could he deliver on the grandest stage without those familiar elements?

Reigns and CM Punk answered with a story-heavy match built around two questions: Could Punk still hang with an athlete like Reigns, and could The OTC beat The Best in the World without outside help?

The answer to both was yes. Ultimately, though, Punk's exhaustion proved decisive. He collapsed while attempting another GTS, leaving Reigns to deliver two Spears and capture the World Heavyweight Championship.

The drama was off the charts, the match was outstanding, and the crowd was hot for both men.

It marked the start of a chapter built around Reigns proving his superiority through his own ability rather than outside help. His championship victory provided the foundation for that story.

Over the ensuing months, he delivered some of the best matches of his career against opponents with contrasting styles and backgrounds, placing the emphasis on the wrestling rather than the interference and elaborate twists.

Yet, as great as his WrestleMania 42 encounter with Punk was, one match ranks above it for its historical significance alone.

Reigns entered WrestleMania 40 carrying the longest WWE men's world-title reign since Hulk Hogan's run in the 1980s. His 1,316-day stint as Universal Champion had lasted more than three and a half years, giving an entire generation of fans a championship reign unlike anything WWE had presented in decades.

Having teamed with The Rock to defeat Cody Rhodes and Seth Rollins the night before, securing a Bloodline Rules stipulation for Sunday's main event, Reigns looked capable of escaping Philadelphia with his Undisputed WWE Universal Championship intact.

This time, however, his family could not save him. Jey Uso took out his brother Jimmy, John Cena neutralized Solo Sikoa, and The Undertaker chokeslammed The Rock to hell.

Letting his emotions get the better of him, Reigns struck Rollins with the chair rather than targeting Rhodes. That decision proved costly, as The American Nightmare delivered three consecutive Cross Rhodes to finish his story and capture the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship.

Reigns lost the match and the title, but the defeat provided a fitting climax to a story that had begun nearly four years earlier. His run helped define a boom period for WWE, culminating in an unforgettable Rhodes victory that signaled a new era for the company.

articles.title: Doncic busca la corona
articles.standfirst: Versus lo sitúa, prácticamente, empatado con Wembanyama para llevarse el MVP
articles.summary: Versus lo sitúa, prácticamente, empatado con Wembanyama para llevarse el MVP
articles.body: Los Lakers viven su mejor momento de la temporada. La victoria de esta madrugada ante los Suns (123-131), con 43 puntos de Luka Doncic, ha sido la octava consecutiva y deja un balance de 12-2 que nadie esperaba tan pronto. Fueron además el primer equipo de la NBA en llegar a las diez victorias. Con Doncic como motor, el conjunto angelino pelea con los Spurs por el primer puesto del Oeste, y el esloveno se ha convertido en el centro de la conversación sobre el MVP. El mercado de apuestas deportivas de Versus, sin embargo, ve la carrera de otra manera. Victor Wembanyama es el favorito, con una cuota de 2.20, ligeramente por delante de Doncic. El francés, de 22 años, promedia 29 puntos, 12.4 rebotes y 4.5 tapones, y ha firmado partidos con 52 y 40 puntos. Los Spurs encadenaron nueve victorias seguidas y tienen el mismo balance que los Lakers. Su candidatura no se apoya en un solo número, sino en un impacto defensivo que ningún otro jugador de la liga puede igualar. Doncic es el segundo, a cuota 2.35, y la distancia con su rival es mínima. Los números respaldan su candidatura. Lidera la NBA con 38.6 puntos por partido y en noviembre eleva esa media a 40.7. Esta semana firmó 53 puntos ante Portland y 43 anoche ante los Suns, y ha dejado actuaciones como los 32 puntos, 10 asistencias, ocho rebotes y cinco robos ante los Hawks. La clasificación semanal de NBA.com le mantiene en el primer puesto, por delante de Wembanyama, lo que sugiere que parte de la prensa ve la carrera de forma más favorable al esloveno que el mercado de casas de apuestas. Su impacto va más allá de los puntos. Los Lakers han superado a sus rivales por 105 puntos con él en pista durante las seis victorias de noviembre en las que ha jugado. Esa dependencia tiene su cara menos amable. En cinco partidos de octubre, el equipo fue superado por 45 puntos cuando descansaba. Además, Doncic pierde 5.1 balones por partido, la segunda peor cifra de la liga, y tuvo que perderse un encuentro por molestias en la espalda. El susto del miércoles en Milwaukee, con la lesión de varios jugadores, es un recordatorio de que su disponibilidad será clave en la carrera. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander aparece a cuota 13, muy lejos de los dos primeros. El base canadiense sigue siendo un jugador de élite y un candidato permanente, pero su precio refleja que el mercado ha cerrado la pelea a dos nombres. Para que su cuota tenga valor necesitaría un cambio de tendencia importante en las próximas semanas. Jayson Tatum se paga a 15. El alero ha escalado hasta el tercer puesto en la clasificación de NBA.com y es el mejor situado de los aspirantes de segunda fila. Su precio premia la paciencia de quien confíe en que mantendrá su nivel durante toda la temporada, aunque tendrá que recortar una distancia considerable con los dos líderes. Nikola Jokic cierra la lista de favoritos, a cuota 21. El pívot serbio, ganador de tres MVP, es séptimo en la clasificación de NBA.com y ofrece el mayor premio de los cinco. Es un jugador que acostumbra a dejar su mejor versión para el tramo final de la temporada, y por eso su cuota merece un vistazo para los más arriesgados. De cara a las apuestas, conviene recordar que estamos a mediados de noviembre, y que el MVP se decide en abril.

articles.title: BYD y la Fórmula 1: "Seguimos muy interesados, pero es un proceso complicado y se necesita paciencia"
articles.standfirst: Stella Li, vicepresidenta ejecutiva de BYD, charla con MARCA sobre sus ambiciones para la competición y las posibilidades de fabricar sus coches en España
articles.summary: Stella Li, vicepresidenta ejecutiva de BYD, charla con MARCA sobre sus ambiciones para la competición y las posibilidades de fabricar sus coches en España
articles.body: Stella Li (vicepresidenta ejecutiva del grupo BYD) es, hoy por hoy y junto a Mary Barra, CEO de General Motors, la mujer más poderosa del mundo del motor. En sus manos está la gestión del grupo BYD, el ya quinto fabricante mundial de automóviles (según ella mismo reveló), y primero en vehículos eléctricos y de 'nueva energía' (es decir, enchufables, ya sean híbridos o exclusivamente de baterías). MARCA tuvo la ocasión de departir unos minutos con la ejecutiva china en Abu Dhabi, en el marco de la celebración del récord mundial de velocidad del YangWang U9 Xtreme, que consiguió romper por primera vez la barrera de los 500 km/h en un coche de producción. En el emirato también mostró al mundo por primera vez el YangWang Altior, una ambiciosa berlina de representación con la que medirse nada más y nada menos que con los fabricantes especialistas en el máximo lujo, como Bentley o Rolls-Royce. Precisamente esa ambición es lo que mueve a YangWang, la marca que abandera las prestaciones, la tecnología y la exclusividad dentro del grupo BYD. Una marca que debería llegar a Europa a finales de 2027 o principios de 2028 como un paso más allá de lo que ahora propone Denza, que acaba de dar sus primeros pasos en el viejo continente... y también en España. La llegada de YangWang a Europa será el mayor reto para la compañía china, ya que competirá en un mercado mucho más exigente para los asiáticos. Pero Li tiene la estrategia para conseguir convencer también a los compradores de superdeportivos o de coches de ultralujo. "Estamos trabajando muy duro en conseguir llevar al mercado el efecto ¡wow! Queremos que la gente disfrute de la tecnología, por eso ponemos mucho esfuerzo en hacer que se sorprendan con ella", explica. Una sensación que el cliente tiene que experimentar en toda la experiencia con su vehículo: "Tanto cuando se aproximan al coche como cuando lo conducen. Queremos que sientan: 'guau, es mejor que las marcas establecidas'. Ese es un nuestro propósito. SI conseguimos seguir sorprendiendo al mercado tendremos una oportunidad para lograrlo", vaticina. YangWang es el futuro (habrá que ver si llegamos a ver sus productos en España, algo que será complicado porque no son los más indicados para nuestro mercado), pero en el presente BYD sigue avanzando a pasos agigantados en nuestro país, con nuevos modelos y consiguiendo hitos en los ranking de ventas. Lógicamente, el rendimiento de la marca en España es motivo de satisfacción para su máxima ejecutiva: "Estoy muy contenta con los resultados de la marca en España, todos los indicadores muestran que a los españoles les encantan los coches BYD", asegura. Con la marca en pleno proceso de establecerse entre los protagonistas del mercado de los coches electrificados, el siguiente paso de expansión podría ser la fabricación en nuestro país, algo que Li no descarta: "España está en una lista corta de candidatos para nuestra futura expansión de fabricación", asegura. Un paso que le falta por dar al fabricante chino es el de lanzarse a la competición... aunque es algo que está en los planes de presente y futuro. Y esa entrada podría ser por todo lo alto: nada menos que en la Fórmula 1. No es un secreto que el fabricante chino está en conversaciones con la categoría reina del automovilismo mundial para poder formar parte de ella en el futuro, conversaciones que la vicepresidenta ejecutiva de BYD asegura que siguen su curso, pero que necesitan tiempo. "BYD continúa explorando esa opción, pero está claro que es un proceso muy complicado y que se necesita ser paciente para trabajarlo. Pero estamos muy interesados y seguimos explorándolo, sí". Y el mensaje final, para cuando llegue ese momento, es claro: "Tendremos la misma ambición en la competición que en la industria"

articles.title: Jim Ratcliffe's Ineos Group settles £10m-plus claim with Sir Ben Ainslie's Athena Racing over alleged non-return of yacht
articles.summary: Ineos Racing sued Athena Racing earlier this year, alleging the latter breached a deal between the two companies by refusing to return multimillion-pound yacht; Sir Ben Ainslie's GB1 team is the challenger of record for the next America's Cup in Naples, Italy in 2027
articles.body:
Ineos Racing sued Athena Racing earlier this year, alleging the latter breached a deal between the two companies by refusing to return the multimillion-pound yacht Ineos Britannia, which Ainslie captained at the 2024 America's Cup in a 7-2 defeat to Emirates Team New Zealand in Barcelona.

Lawyers for Ineos said in court documents filed earlier this year that the claim was valued at more than £10 million.

Athena Racing was defending the claim, arguing that Ineos was not entitled to have the yacht back.

In a statement on Monday, Ineos said: "Ineos has reached a settlement with Athena Racing and considers the matter now closed."

No further details, including whether the yacht has been returned, have been provided.

Four-time Olympic champion Ainslie hit out at Ineos Britannia in April 2025 after they confirmed their challenge for the 38th America's Cup in Naples in 2027 would not involve him.

Ainslie's GB1 team is the challenger of record for the event in Italy next year.

No British team has ever won the America's Cup since it was first contested in 1850.

articles.title: Connor McDavid matched Wayne Gretzky’s historic NHL record during Edmonton Oilers’ impressive victory over Philadelphia Flyers
articles.summary: Connor McDavid matches Wayne Gretzky’s 42-year-old record by achieving 40 assists in 22 games during the Edmonton Oilers' 5-2 victory against the Philadelphia Flyers, solidifying his status as the league's leading scorer.
articles.body: Connor McDavid has matched Wayne Gretzky’s 42-year-old NHL record with 40 assists in 22 games as the Edmonton Oilers defeated the Philadelphia Flyers 5-2. The milestone gave McDavid a 22-game point streak to start the season and further solidified him as the league’s leading scorer.The Edmonton captain finished with a goal and two assists, giving him 53 points on the season. His feat also highlighted the Oilers’ hot streak, as the club pushed its winning streak to five straight.Connor McDavid matches Wayne Gretzky’s historic NHL assists recordConnor McDavid became the fastest player in NHL history to reach 40 assists in a season, doing so in 22 games to match Wayne Gretzky.Gretzky set the mark in the 1984-85 season, and it’s a point of pride for the Edmonton Oilers legend that he was able to make such a statement in an era when he had a stranglehold on the game. McDavid’s latest milestone puts him in the NHL record books as one of the greatest players in hockey.The 29-year-old captain reached the mark in a three-point game that included an assist against the Philadelphia Flyers. He then went on to 41 assists in 22 appearances, bringing his total points in scoring to 53.How did McDavid achieve the milestone against Philadelphia?McDavid hit the historic milestone in a dominant performance against the Philadelphia Flyers at Xfinity Mobile Arena. The Edmonton Oilers secured a 5-2 road win, and their captain was right in the middle of it all.The Canadian forward finished with an empty-net goal and two assists for three points. His goal allowed Edmonton to take control of the game, despite a Philadelphia push in the second period.The Oilers took a 3-0 lead in the opening period before the Flyers scored twice in the second period to cut the deficit. Edmonton responded with two goals in the third period to get the win.Leon Draisaitl was also exceptional, notching a pair of goals and adding an assist. Edmonton’s other goal scorers were Vasily Podkolzin and Zach Hyman, while Cole Knuble and Noah Cates scored for Philadelphia.Tristan Jarry made 34 saves for the Oilers, and Edmonton's penalty-killing unit successfully defended all eight Philadelphia power plays. Special teams also proved important in preserving the team's advantage.Why is Wayne Gretzky's record significant for Connor McDavid?The standard set by Wayne Gretzky in 1984-85 is one of the most incredible feats in NHL history. A prolific scorer throughout his career, highlighted by a 40-assist performance in only 22 games.McDavid matching that record is even more meaningful because Gretzky is synonymous with the greatest championship era in the Edmonton Oilers’ history. Both have played for the same franchise and demonstrated great playmaking ability.The Edmonton Oilers have been on a great run of wins that have coincided with McDavid’s record-breaking performance. The win against Philadelphia was their fifth consecutive, further cementing their place near the top of the NHL standings.McDavid has 12 goals and 41 assists for 53 points in 22 games, topping the league. He also has a 22-game point streak to start the season, with a point in each game he’s played so far.McDavid’s latest feat is just another milestone in an already illustrious career. Matching Gretzky’s legendary mark in just 22 games makes him one of the NHL’s most dominant offensive forces, giving Edmonton one more reason to celebrate the remarkable consistency of its captain.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Sir Jim Ratcliffe's Ineos group settles a High Court claim with Sir Ben Ainslie's Athena Racing over a £180m boat used in the America's Cup.
articles.body:
Sir Jim Ratcliffe's Ineos group has settled a High Court claim with Sir Ben Ainslie's Athena Racing over a £180m boat used in the America's Cup.

Ineos took legal steps against Athena Racing in March to secure the return of the boat - named Britannia - after alleging Ainslie's firm had breached a deal between the two companies.

Ratcliffe's petrochemicals company funded two America's Cup cycles led by four-time Olympic champion Ainslie in Auckland in 2021 and Barcelona two years ago.

However, relations between the Manchester United co-owner and Ainslie reportedly turned sour and they split in January 2025, with plans to challenge for the 38th America's Cup in Naples in 2027 abandoned three months later.

In a statement on Monday, an Ineos spokesperson said they had reached a settlement with Athena Racing and "considers the matter now closed".

Meanwhile, Athena confirmed the team has ownership of the multimillion-pound boat. "Athena Racing/GB1 have always been, and remain, the owners of their assets," a statement read.

Ineos blamed the decision to split with Athena on "a protracted negotiation", claiming Ainslie's team had caused a costly six-month delay to settlement talks.

Ainslie became Ineos Britannia's team principal and skipper when he received the backing of Britain's largest privately-owned company in 2018 in a bid to win sailing's oldest prize - something Great Britain had never done before.

In 2024, the team led by Ainslie, 49, reached the final of the 37th edition in Barcelona for the first time since 1964, but they were beaten 7-2 by defending champions New Zealand.

Following the fallout with Ratcliffe, Ainslie secured private equity funding for Athena from Oakley Capital and rebranded the team as GB1 in January.

articles.title: Belgium’s Romelu Lukaku retires from international football
articles.summary: Lukaku is Belgium’s all-time leading goalscorer with 94 goals in 135 games and is fifth on men’s all-time scoring list.
articles.body:
Romelu Lukaku, Belgium’s all-time leading goalscorer, has announced his retirement from international football after 16 years, saying he was “at peace” with his decision.

“These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team. It was a nice ride and I enjoyed every single moment,” Belgium’s record goalscorer said on Instagram on Monday.

With 94 goals in 135 games, Lukaku is the fifth-highest scorer in men’s international football history and featured in four World Cups for the Red Devils, helping them reach the quarterfinals of this year’s tournament before losing to eventual winners Spain.

The 33-year-old, who now plays for Turkish club Fenerbahce, made his debut in 2010 as a teenager and was an unused substitute in Sunday’s 4-1 Nations League win over Italy.

“To the Belgium fans, thank you for the support you gave our team. I am proud to have represented my country in 4 World Cups and 3 European Championships.

“I will never forget those moments. I’m at peace with my decision to stop here,” Lukaku said.

The former Chelsea, Manchester United and Inter Milan forward was part of Belgium’s so-called “golden generation”.

Lukaku, alongside Kevin De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, finished third at the 2018 World Cup, a best-ever finish for Belgium in the tournament, but they failed to lift a trophy during the period.

“I played with amazing teammates that I will always be grateful for,” Lukaku said.

“I want to thank them all. I want to thank all the coaches as well for pushing and trusting me to help the team,” he added.

Inspiration to generations of football fans

The national team paid homage to Lukaku shortly after his announcement.

“More than a goalscorer, you have been a leader, a strong personality and an inspiration to generations of Belgian football fans,” said a post on Instagram by the Red Devils. “You have written an incredible chapter in the history of the Red Devils.”

A host of fellow Belgian players also paid tribute to Lukaku.

“Legend, my brother,” midfielder Axel Witsel posted on Instagram.

“Thank you for everything my bro,” Courtois said.

“So many amazing memories,” the Real Madrid goalkeeper added.

Lukaku’s last appearance for his country came in October’s 4-1 loss to France.

“Beyond his exceptional performances on the pitch, he has been a true leader, with a strong personality and an essential role in the dressing room,” Lukaku’s former teammate and now Belgium’s technical director, Simon Mignolet, said in a statement from the Belgian football association.

“We respect his decision and are deeply grateful to him for everything he has brought to our national team,” the former Liverpool goalkeeper added.

Belgium’s first game without Lukaku will be a Nations League last-eight fixture in March.

“We must now turn our attention to the future and prepare for the Nations League quarterfinals … with the ambition of continuing to make progress as a team,” Mignolet said.

articles.title: Leo Harlem propone a Luis de la Fuente como MVP del año: "Me parece un auténtico genio"
articles.standfirst: El humorista reconoce en Radio MARCA que el 2-0 de Escocia le hizo dudar del seleccionador y ahora le ve como candidato a personaje deportivo del año
articles.summary: El humorista reconoce en Radio MARCA que el 2-0 de Escocia le hizo dudar del seleccionador y ahora le ve como candidato a personaje deportivo del año
articles.body: Leo Harlem no olvida lo que pensó cuando España perdió 2-0 en Escocia, en uno de los primeros partidos de Luis de la Fuente como seleccionador. "No daba un duro por él cuando empezó", reconoció en Radio MARCA. Aquel resultado le dejó una primera impresión que hoy recuerda con humor: "¡Ay, mamá, qué mal se pone la cosa!". Su opinión ha cambiado hasta el punto de que, preguntado por si De la Fuente podría ser el personaje del año, Harlem apenas dudó. "Para mí, en el ámbito deportivo, por supuesto. Desde luego que sí, me parece un auténtico genio". Harlem destacó la forma de llevar el cargo del seleccionador. "Dentro de este ámbito deportivo, que estamos todos muy locos, es un tío bastante sensato", explicó. Y tiró de humor para acordarse de otros dos técnicos de la selección: "Los seleccionadores que se llaman Luis o Vicente nos vienen muy bien". Se refería a Luis Aragonés y Vicente del Bosque. Al preguntarle qué es lo que más le gusta de España, Harlem puso el foco en el juego colectivo y en el ambiente del vestuario. "Ya tenemos por fin como un estilo de jugar", apuntó. "Eso es muy importante, no ir a bandazos". El humorista también destacó la juventud de la plantilla y el nivel de los futbolistas que vienen de la sub-21 y la sub-19. "Yo confío en que tengamos bastantes años de alegrías", concluyó.

articles.title: Jordan Scott injury means Michigan State must dig into its depth vs. Tennessee
articles.summary: Jordan Scott's shoulder injury isn't structural, but it could hold him out of Michigan State's visit to Tennessee on Tuesday.
articles.body:
EAST LANSING — Right after Jordan Scott put together one of the most dominant defensive performances by a Michigan State player in years in a Nov. 10 win over Duke, the sophomore wing suffered a right shoulder injury Nov. 13 against Northern Iowa.

MSU coach Tom Izzo ballparked between 60 and 70 percent odds that Scott might play in No. 5 Michigan State's visit to No. 9 Tennessee on Tuesday, Nov. 17. He provided an update Monday that there is no structural damage to Scott's shoulder, but he has been held out of contact drills and practice.

"Your guess is as good as mine, except that I think he's going to be all right," Izzo said Nov. 16. "... It just depends on how fast it comes along, to be very honest with you. He's got a decent range of motion now, it's whether he gets a bump again, what'll happen, and what doesn't happen."

This Michigan State team is equipped to deal with some misfortune on the injury front. It's deep, and even though Scott has been one of its best players — maybe as good as or better than All-American point guard Jeremy Fears Jr. — Izzo has some options. Coen Carr started at the three most of last season. Shooting guard Kur Teng has also worked in there for spare reps as more of a traditional wing. Izzo hinted that freshman combo guard C.J. Medlock might mix in on the wings, too.

Shouldering the brunt of the extra workload for Michigan State (4-0) will likely be fellow wing Kaleb Glenn, whose return from a knee injury that shelved him all of last season has had a slower acclimation the past couple of games, particularly on the defensive end where MSU's gap scheme differs from what he used to run at Florida Atlantic two years ago. Part of Izzo's plan is to keep Glenn at small forward alone, as opposed to mixing in at power forward where Carr and Cam Ward are handling most of the minutes. The two had a meeting to "speed that process" of defensive acclimation up.

"That's kind of hard when you haven't played for a year and you come back and now you're trying to learn two positions. So we've kind of tried to simplify that a little bit," Izzo said. "But I keep telling him he's built like Adonis. He's gotta play like it. And he goes to the offensive boards better than anybody, and that's encouraging."

Michigan State turns to Glenn in what should be another strong test in the early non-conference slate. Tennessee (3-0) struggled with Tennessee State last week but made the past three Elite Eights and was projected preseason to finish fourth in the SEC. Rick Barnes has 13 new players this season, nine of them transfers.

"This will be a challenge," Izzo said. "It'll be a challenge because it's down there. It'll be a challenge because the place will be rocking, and it'll be a challenge because they're going to be maybe as physical a team as we (have) played so far."

Playing in a road environment should be a test for Michigan State, which faced Duke in a friendly neutral site at Chicago's United Center and played Marquette in a semi-neutral site exhibition at Fiserv Stadium in Milwaukee. This is a venue that should put the Spartans — and Glenn — into the fire.

"He's going to get more of an opportunity as it is because he's earned it," Izzo said. "But if Jordan doesn't play, he'll get a lot more opportunity."

▶ Tip : 9 p.m., Tuesday, Nov. 17, Food City Center, Knoxville, Tenn.

▶ Records : No. 3 Michigan State 4-0; No. 14 Tennessee 3-0

▶ Series : MSU leads, 5-2. Last meeting: Michigan State won, 70-69, in the Elite Eight on March 28, 2010.

articles.title: Jaguars coach Liam Coen on winning road games, defensive struggles
articles.summary: Highlights of Jaguars coach Liam Coen's news conference a day after they played the Tennessee Titans.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars coach Liam Coen met with the media in a virtual news conference on Nov. 16 to discuss the team's 40-23 victory over the Tennessee Titans the day before, in Nashville.

The Jaguars (7-2) have a four-game lead over the Houston Texans in the AFC South. They will play their third road game and their sixth game in seven way from Jacksonville on Nov. 22 when they face the New York Giants in East Rutherford, N.J. (4:25 p.m., CBS).

(Note: Coen is 9-3 in road games as the Jaguars coach)

"I thought they handled the week really well. Professional. You've got to go win division games on the road. For us to have to play four quarters ...we hadn't really had to play four quarters since Houston, so that was good for us to get some of that experience, the offense closing a game out for the first time in a while in four minutes was important. But I thought our guys handled it the right way in a good week of preparation."

Liam Coen on the play of backup center Jonah Monheim

(Note: Starting center Robert Hainsey left the game with a knee injury)

"Very mature. Jonah's only a second-year player, but he's very mature, takes things seriously, but doesn't overcook it either. Doesn't try to overdo it. Obviously played at a high level at USC, and that's good football. He's been in big games. He's been in big moments. He played big. And then I think his preparation throughout the week, learning from Hainsey and that group, and the communication ... he gets a lot of reps during the week as well, whether it's stealing those reps in blitz protection, walkthroughs and practice, he gets a lot of reps. So we have a lot of confidence in Jonah."

Liam Coen on RB Bhayshul Tuten's heavy workload vs. Titans

"I don't know if he was feeling 100 percent yesterday. And some runs that I think he normally either breaks or gets extra yards on didn't quite occur yesterday. But I mean 26 [carries] was his biggest workload that he's had over the year. The average [per carry, 3.4 yards] wasn't where we'd like to be but to be able to still have [26] rushes in that kind of game ... you have to be able to run the ball when you have a lead and then when you get a two-score lead, you're continuing to want to run the football better.

"But the fact that he's doing this and playing and giving us this many snaps with limited practice ... this is really cool. It speaks to the guy, how tough he is, how competitive he is. I've been very pleased with his professionalism and consistency."

(Note: Jordan Davis will likely play against the Giants and B.J. Green is practicing again)

"We just look at what those matchups are [vs. the Giants offensive line] and which ones we want to go try to attack this week, and whether that's getting B.J. up and giving him an opportunity or if it's another week of seeing what it looks like. I think, organically, some of the things will occur on the front. We'll have to look at it throughout the course of this week. Somebody's going to not be able to be active, and who that is, we're not quite sure, being so early in the game planning process for New York. We'll have a little bit of a better feel, I'd assume by Wednesday, Thursday, see what it looks like. B.J. had a good week of practice last week, getting back into the swing of things. He's eager, he's hungry, he wants to get out there and play for us."

Liam Coen on players other than captains showing leadership

"I think Jahlani Tavai on special team. Dennis Gardeck as well, Ventrell Miller specifically as well. I think Walker Little , in his own way, has been a presence for those guys on the offensive side of the football. Quintin Morris is a guy that leads ... Buster Brown , he leads in his own ways. That's a handful of guys ... that are not captains that are leaders. Those are the next guys, right? That you continue to spread the leadership to and the message to, and they can help get the message along.

(Note: Coen became the third NFL coach after Matt LaFleur and Sean McVay to win 20 of his first 26 games in the last 15 years).

"It's so early in a tenure it's hard to celebrate anything because you just don't even feel like you've accomplished anything yet. And it's great to keep winning. I think it's a cool deal for us to just keep winning in different ways as a team, different guys stepping up and making plays, while also some of our household names are making big plays for us. The group of guys that we're able to work with on a day-to-day basis, not just the coaching staff, but the entire building and support staff is very much aligned, which makes this whole process that much more enjoyable.

"That's what I honestly celebrate. That is the vision, obviously, that you tried to have coming in. Is every single play perfect? No. That's the beauty of football. But I believe we have a connected building. And I think that's something that I actually celebrate and enjoy."

"I don't think it was our best . I'm not sure we swarmed and ran to the ball quite as much as I would like to see us do at times. Kind of at times, looked like we were trying to punch the ball out instead of getting the guy on the ground a few times. But I thought for the most part guys played well. It wasn't perfect. We can play better, but our defense played really well. I think the last few weeks we have held teams under 20 points a lot ... and we should win games if they play that way."

Liam Coen on the team struggling vs. the Titans

"This game, in my opinion ... I kind of felt like this was going to be a game where Tennessee might be able to move the ball and do some things. They've been getting better on offense and trending in that direction, and so kind of knew we were going to have to score some points. And I wanted to see our offense go. We talked the last few weeks about, 'man, we're leaving points out on the grass, and we still did yesterday. The red zone multiple times, we left points out there. I'm glad that we were tested. I'm glad that we had to play four quarters and go close a game out the right way. There's a lot to keep coaching off of."

articles.title: Phil Taylor and Raymond van Barneveld to renew their iconic rivalry as non-playing captains at pro-celeb event at Alexandra Palace
articles.summary: Phil Taylor and Raymond van Barneveld set to collide almost 20 years since their iconic world championship final; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports up until the final on November 22
articles.body:
Two of darts' greatest names will lead teams featuring world champions and celebrity guests on Thursday December 10, with £5 from every ticket sold donated to Prostate Cancer UK.

Taylor and Van Barneveld famously contested the 2007 final at the Circus Tavern in Purfleet, one of the sport's most memorable matches.

Almost 20 years on, they will bring that competitive spirit to the captaincy as their teams battle for the Rivals Reunited trophy.

The evening will serve as a test event ahead of the World's move into Alexandra Palace's larger Great Hall, giving fans an early opportunity to experience the new setting before the venue hosts the tournament for the 20th time.

Phil Taylor said: "Raymond and I have had some great battles over the years, and the competitive instinct never goes away. It should be a good laugh, but I'll still be making sure my team know we're there to win!"

Raymond van Barneveld added: "Phil says it's a bit of fun, but I know what he's like - he'll want to win just as much as I do! It will be great to be back at Ally Pally together, and hopefully my team can give the fans plenty to cheer about."

Two-time world champion Adrian Lewis, radio presenter Jordan North and social media personality Woody, will feature for Team Taylor.

Team Barney will include three-time world champion John Part, radio presenter Chris Stark and comedian Lloyd Griffith.

articles.title: Anthony Davis trade is top of mind after shameful Rockets game drops Wizards to 4-10
articles.summary: The Washington Wizards grew tired of a traditional rebuild and attempted to end their residence in the NBA’s abyss by adding established stars Anthony Davis...
articles.body:
The Washington Wizards grew tired of a traditional rebuild and attempted to end their residence in the NBA's abyss by adding established stars Anthony Davis and Trae Young. The risks were obvious given the players' respective injury histories, but if healthy, they were supposed to lead the franchise to far more competitive results. Well, it appears another blueprint just got put through the shredder.

Young has played in all 14 of the Wizards' games this season. Davis has suited up for 12. They were both on the floor for Sunday's home matchup versus the Houston Rockets, and yet, Washington treated its fans to a humiliating 147-119 loss . The team is now 4-10. Despite fan optimism that the Will Dawkins-led front office had a feasible plan in place, this organization is eliciting the same feelings of misery roughly a month into the campaign.

The best way for the Wizards to foster genuine hope is to prioritize their young crop of talent and stockpile draft picks. They already committed to Young via a $212 million-plus contract extension, but there is no reason to believe that Davis will be part of their long-term plans. A trade is becoming more plausible every time this squad takes the court. Is a midseason split inevitable? The Fullcourtpass X account is posing that very question .

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The future Hall of Famer carries a hefty $62.79 million player option for the 2027-28 season, but if he can stay relatively healthy and continue to have a two-way impact, suitors could emerge. Anthony Davis is averaging 24.7 points, 10.3 rebounds, 1.3 steals and 1.1 blocks per contest, while also shooting 51.6 percent from the field and 32.1 percent from 3-point range. Those beefy numbers have not improved Washington's fortunes, however.

Following an encouraging 4-3 start, the Wizards have now dropped seven straight and surrendered 120 or more points five times in that span. The 33-year-old big man is still a force to be reckoned with, but apparently, the team is not presently equipped to capitalize on his skill set. Unless Washington enjoys a drastic turnaround, management will need to strongly consider trading Davis and emphasizing guys like AJ Dybantsa, Kyshawn George, Alex Sarr and others.

If the futility persists, perhaps The Brow will take it upon himself to seek an escape.

articles.title: Rams Week 10 snap counts: 50-50 split at RB, new WR tandem emerges
articles.summary: Blake Corum and Kyren Williams played the same number of snaps, while Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels were the Rams' top two WRs on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams had to shuffle the deck on offense Sunday, and the results were even better than expected. Despite being without Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Terrance Ferguson and Steve Avila, the Rams put up their second-most points of the season in a 34-6 win .

They had to dig deep at wide receiver and along the offensive line, while the defense remained a top-five unit once again with a performance not seen in Rams history since 1977 .

The snap counts from Sunday's win show how many different players contributed, from Blake Corum and CJ Daniels to Bill Murray and Emmanuel Forbes Jr. Here's a breakdown of the playing time from the Rams' fourth straight win, where the split at running back was 50-50 and Daniels emerged as a starting receiver alongside Konata Mumpfield.

A lot of people were wondering how the Rams would replace Nacua, Adams and Jordan Whittington at wide receiver. The answer was Mumpfield and Daniels, with a dash of Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith. Mumpfield and Daniels played 63% and 61% of the snaps, respectively, with Atwell only playing 21%. Many expected Atwell to be a top receiver now but he's still playing a specific role on offense. Smith played nine snaps in his return, catching two passes for 40 yards and a touchdown.

At running back, Blake Corum and Kyren Williams each played exactly 39 snaps, and it's not because the score was so lopsided. If anything, Corum got most of the meaningful snaps while the game was somewhat within reach before Williams and Ronnie Rivers closed it out. This is the closest the Rams have been to a true 1A and 1B in the backfield. Williams is still the starter, but Corum keeps eating into his carries and might be the RB1 now based on his touches.

The Rams had to get creative on the O-line because not only was Steve Avila out, but Coleman Shelton and Dylan McMahon both got hurt. That forced Beaux Limmer to start at left guard and eventually moved to center after Shelton and McMahon went down, thrusting Bill Murray into the game at left guard. Shelton played 17 snaps before getting hurt and McMahon exited after just 12 plays.

With Ferguson still out, the Rams still leaned on their tight ends heavily. Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen and Tyler Higbee all played between 67% and 70% of the snaps, with Parkinson leading the way. Max Klare played four snaps, as well.

Quentin Lake was the only player to take 100% of the snaps, which is atypical but the Rams wanted to give their defenders a break in such a lopsided game. Kam Curl still played 86% of the snaps and Kam Kinchens played 71%, so the safeties were still on the field a bunch.

Josh Wallace and Trent McDuffie were the top two cornerbacks, playing 86% of the snaps. Emmanuel Forbes Jr. operated as the No. 3 corner, playing 60%, with Cam Lampkin coming in for one snap.

There's an interesting development happening at inside linebacker. Shaun Dolac continues to eat into Omar Speights and Nate Landman's snaps, playing 37% of the snaps on Sunday. That's the same share Speights had (37%) and was only seven plays fewer than Landman had. Are the Rams beginning to take snaps away from Landman in favor of Dolac?

Myles Garrett wasn't needed very much in the blowout win, only playing 17 snaps. Byron Young led the edge rushers with a 63% snap share. Wesley Bailey continues to get his opportunities, playing 43% of the snaps.

The defensive line was led by none other than Aaron Donald, who had a 66% snap share. Tyler Davis played 63%, Braden Fiske played 57% and Ty Hamilton played 43%. Larrell Murchison played nine snaps, too.

articles.title: Jahmyr Gibbs Is Chasing an NFL Record Untouched Since 2009
articles.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs has eight games to take down a record that has stood since 2009. #OnePride
articles.body:
Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs needs 140.8 yards from scrimmage per game across Detroit's final eight games to break the NFL's single-season record. He is averaging 153.8.

Gibbs has 1,384 yards from scrimmage through nine games, built on 1,000 rushing yards on 199 carries at 5.0 per attempt and 384 receiving yards on 41 catches. The single-season record belongs to Chris Johnson , who put up 2,509 yards for the Tennessee Titans in 2009 on 2,006 rushing and 503 receiving, a number nobody has reached in the 17 seasons since .

Sunday in Munich was the kind of afternoon that makes the math work. Gibbs ran for 153 yards and caught passes for 99 more in Detroit's 35-10 win over the New England Patriots , a 252-yard scrimmage day that also pushed him into rare company on the touchdown list .

What Jahmyr Gibbs Needs Over the Final Eight Games

The gap is 1,126 yards. Spread across eight games, that is 140.8 per week, and Gibbs is currently clearing that number by 13 yards a game. Hold the current pace through a 17-game season and he finishes at 2,614, the same total Underdog has him projected for .

Pace is not a promise. A projection assumes eight more healthy games and a workload nobody trims, and Detroit has reason to be careful with a back who already has 240 touches. But the margin is real rather than theoretical, and he does not need a career week to get there. He needs the week he has been having.

Detroit's Backfield Belongs to Gibbs Now

The split that used to cap Gibbs is gone. David Montgomery is in Houston, where he sits second on the Texans depth chart and is currently listed out, and nothing behind Gibbs in Detroit has replaced that role. Sione Vaki is next on the Lions in carries with 36 for 163 yards , Jacob Saylors sits third, and Isiah Pacheco is on injured reserve.

That is the part of this chase that separates Gibbs from most backs who have flirted with the record. He is not splitting a committee down the middle. He has 199 of Detroit's carries and 41 of its receptions, and the only thing standing between him and the volume is a coaching staff deciding he has had enough on a given afternoon.

Christian McCaffrey Came Closest, and the 17th Game Matters

The last back to get into range was Christian McCaffrey , who finished 2019 with the Carolina Panthers at 2,392 yards from scrimmage, 1,387 rushing and 1,005 receiving, in a 16-game season. Johnson's 2009 total also broke a record that had stood for a decade, Marshall Faulk's 2,429 for the St. Louis Rams in 1999.

The schedule helps. Johnson and Faulk set their marks in 16-game seasons, and McCaffrey fell 117 short with the same number of games. Gibbs gets a 17th, an extra week of production neither of them had. On the way he is going he may not need it.

articles.title: Report card: Jets lose 31-12 vs. Bills in Week 10
articles.summary: Grading the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills in Week 10
articles.body:
The New York Jets suffered their fifth-straight loss in a row, 31-12, to the Buffalo Bills (8-1) on Sunday. The loss puts the Jets at 2-8 in a game that was basically rinse and repeat from the previous week.

For Buffalo, it was their fifth win in a row as they are pulling away in the AFC East.

The Jets played well in the first half, but once again settled for too many field goals and that simply won't cut it against the Bills. They also suffered a few injuries as quarterback Geno Smith and receiver Omar Cooper Jr. were hurt. Smith suffered an ankle injury and was evaluated for a concussion . Head coach Aaron Glenn had no update after the game on Smith's condition.

Here is Jets Wire's report for the team's Week 10 loss to the Bills :

Smith wasn't exactly setting the world on fire with his numbers as he finished with only 148 yards passing. He left the game after suffering an ankle injury right before halftime. Rookie Cade Klubnik took over in the second half and led the Jets to a field goal that cut the deficit to one point, but struggled the rest of the game. He was sacked three times and threw an ugly interception. It's tough to criticize Klubnik as he was put in a tough spot against a very good Bills team.

If we're going to praise Garrett Wilson when he does well, we also need to criticize him when he makes a mistake. GW finished with 106 yards on seven catches, but fumbled the ball on an ill-advised lateral attempt in the red zone to Kenyon Sadiq that was recovered by the Bills. A touchdown on that drive would have cut the deficit to four had they went for two. Instead, they got no points.

Between the two, Braelon Allen was the better runner on the afternoon as he finished with 40 yards on eight carries. Breece Hall had 41 yards on 11 carries and hasn't rushed for 100 yards since Week 1. I understand the need to give Hall carries, but Allen really needs to be the featured back in this offense until further notice. Hall was actually strong in the receiving game with four catches for 64 yards. Klubnik showed off his running ability with 26 yards on three carries.

In all fairness, the Jets did a pretty good job not letting Josh Allen beat them through the air. Yes, he did connect with DJ Moore on a deep touchdown early in the third quarter, but Allen only threw for 191 yards, that touchdown and an interception. Outside of the Moore touchdown, the Bills receivers were relatively quiet on the afternoon and Azareye'h Thomas had his first career interception and the Jets second of the season. David Bailey had a very quiet day with only one tackle, but Will McDonald had the only sack for the Jets, his fourth of the season.

James Cook destroyed the Jets run defense to the tune of 157 yards on 18 carries and an average of just under nine yards per carry. His 74 yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter sealed the victory for the Bills. Josh Allen also had a rushing touchdown and the two now have 19 touchdowns combined between them on the ground. Buffalo rushed for over 200 yards as the woes for the Jets defensive line continue in stopping the run.

Jason Sanders had four more field goals on the afternoon and accounted for all of the Jets points in this game. Sanders has only missed one field goal in the month of November and has only missed three all season.

There's nothing more that needs to be said about the performance of this team. It was the second week in a row where the Jets played a strong first half and then basically quit in the second half. They are simply not aggressive enough when they need to be and it sure looks like Glenn doesn't coach to win games, but more to prevent mistakes.

Frank Reich has been a disaster as an offensive coordinator as the Jets have not scored a touchdown in nine quarters. It feels almost improbable that a team with a talented group of wide receivers as well as two good running backs can't put the ball in the end zone or devise a game plan against a Bills defense that allows over 330 yards per game to score touchdowns.

The Jets are not going to fire Glenn, but it may be time to give Reich his walking papers. It is simply inexcusable for an offensive coordinator (especially a veteran like Reich) to not get the most out of his talent, even with the injury to Smith. It won't happen, so I won't hold my breath but the Jets are officially back to being unwatchable again, which should frustrate everyone at One Jets Drive the same way it frustrates a fan base that wastes their Sunday afternoons putting up with this garbage.

The next seven games are going to feel like an eternity and it's tough to know if they'll even see another win before the season is over. That may be the best thing going for them at this point so it prevents false hope that Glenn and this terrible coaching staff will actually turn it around to be back in 2027.

articles.title: UFL's BattleHawks work out a deal to stay at dome in St. Louis
articles.summary: As of last month, the UFL had a stadium issue in St.
articles.body:
As of last month, the UFL had a stadium issue in St. Louis. As of now, it's resolved.

Via Fox 2 in St. Louis, the UFL and the powers-that-be have struck a deal to create better flexibility in the scheduling of five BattleHawks home games at The Dome at America's Center.

Under the prior schedule, the BattleHawks would have played four straight home games, followed by five straight road games, capped by a home game. The details of the revised schedule have not yet been announced.

UFL co-owner Mike Repole, who has been aggressively using Twitter to market the league and to squabble directly with critics, took a social-media victory lap.

" We weren't going to settle ," he posted. "We pushed for better. We got it done!!!! A BIG THANK YOU to our partners at The Dome at America's Center."

While the UFL is largely a made-for-TV league, it has been trying to create better visuals by playing in stadiums that are easier to fill. The size of the dome in St. Louis makes that harder. Stacking four home games together in four straight weekends won't make that any easier.

articles.title: Akron men's soccer earns No. 4 NCAA Tournament seed for third time in program history
articles.summary: The Zips earned the fourth spot in the 48-team NCAA Tournament bracket after claiming the Big East tournament with wins over Creighton and Georgetown.
articles.body:
Kick the door hard enough and eventually it caves in.

The Akron men's soccer team did that this season, and the NCAA selection committee rewarded the Zips by making them the No. 4 overall seed in its 48-team bracket. Pairings were announced Nov. 16.

It's the third time Akron has been the No. 4 in the tournament.

That's despite the fact the Zips ended the season as the No. 1-ranked team in the nation (the first time since Aug. 30, 2016).

Photos: NCAA men's soccer, Akron Zips vs. Robert Morris

Akron will play the winner of San Diego (11-5-3) or Grand Canyon (13-5-2) at home on Nov. 22.

This is the eighth time the Zips have been a top-five seed in the tournament since they went from regional pairings to seeded pairings in 1994 — No. 1 in 2009, No. 3 in 2010, No. 4 in 2015 and 2016, and No. 5 in 2008, 2012 and 2017.

It's also the 13th time Akron has had a seed — No. 9 in 2005, No. 14 in 2007 and 2025, No. 15 in 2003 and No. 16 2022.

When Akron men's soccer was seeded in the NCAA Tournament

Why Akron claimed the No. 4 seed in the NCAA Tournament

We'll start with the Zips playing in the Big East, arguably the toughest league in the nation.

Then we'll add the fact they beat No. 8 Creighton 4-0 in the Big East Tournament and followed it up with a 1-0 overtime win over No. 2 Georgetown in the championship. By the way, the Hoyas (15-2-2) picked up the No. 1 overall seed.

The Zips' shutout win over Georgetown was the first time the Hoyas had been shut out in 30 games, since a 1-0 loss to Maryland on Aug. 25, 2025.

Incidentally, if the seeds hold out, Akron would play Georgetown in the College Cup in Cary, N.C. on Dec. 11 with the winner advancing to the title match on Dec. 14.

Why the seed is a testament to Jared Embick and the Zips

The Zips' 13-1-4 record this season (.833) is coach Jared Embick's best record, eclipsing 2015 when the 14-year head coach took Akron (18-3-3, .813) to the College Cup.

Embick is 218-88-51 in his collegiate head coaching career, including 171-67-43 at Akron, making him the winningest coach in program history. Ken Lolla's teams went 160-68-25 from 1993-2005.

articles.title: Hawks’ Frontcourt Woes Put Mo Gueye Right In Position To Start
articles.summary: With Okongwu and Landale struggling from deep, Hawks coach Quin Snyder may have to turn to Mouhamed Gueye if he can fix his shot.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Hawks are stuck in a rough patch, and the blame lands squarely on their big men who cannot hit a three-pointer. Head coach Quin Snyder admits the team failed to play with force at the start of recent games, which hurt their defense. This lack of intensity has left the team reeling after two straight close losses, including an overtime defeat to Chicago on Friday. The frontcourt rotation is broken, and the solution might be sitting on the bench waiting for a chance.

Per Soaring Down South , the team's struggles are clear when looking at the shooting numbers of the current starters. Onyeka Okongwu is converting just 32% of his deep shots, while Jock Landale sits at a poor 22% from beyond the arc. These low percentages have forced the Hawks into early deficits that are hard to overcome. The team needs a different look in the paint, one that can stretch the floor without sacrificing defense. That is exactly where Mouhamed Gueye fits the bill, provided he can finally hit his shot.

Mo Gueye is a drop-dead gorgeous defender, a fact that stands out even without advanced stats. In his 2023 draft class, he ranks second overall in defensive impact, sitting higher than players like Cason Wallace and Anthony Black. Only Victor Wembanyama beats him in that specific category. His ability to guard the rim and switch on the perimeter is already proven. The problem is that his offense has been inconsistent, and his touch inside has sometimes been questionable. He needs to prove he can be a threat from deep to stay on the floor.

If Gueye can raise his career three-point percentage from 29% to even 33%, he becomes impossible to leave out of the rotation. That number would be better than both Okongwu and Landale right now. Quin Snyder needs players who can space the floor, and the current options are failing to do that. Gueye has the physical tools and the defensive mindset to be a starter. He just needs to show he can shoot.

Ironically, Gueye's fractured foot might be the best thing to happen to his young career. He is sidelined until January, which gives him three months of perfect practice time while his teammates struggle to win games. This long layoff allows him to focus entirely on his shooting mechanics without the pressure of game minutes. Despite the Hawks holding a 5-3 record versus Milwaukee across the past two seasons, their present lineup fails to gel. Gueye needs to use this time to fix his shot before he returns.

According to Soaring Down South , the frontcourt is crowded with rookies like Henri Veesaar and Zuby Ejiofor who are promising. Gueye's window to prove himself is narrowing, and this injury might be his last chance to show he belongs. He needs to put it all together for a four-month stretch in early 2027. The team is looking for a winning formula, and a starting five with Gueye at the five could be the answer.
