articles.title: Phillies Predicted To Lose Luis Arraez To Royals, Sign Silver Slugger To Replace Him
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies could lose Luis Arraez this offseason
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies acquired Luis Arraez at the trade deadline, but now he is a free agent and should have plenty of suitors.

Unlike last season, when Arraez had to settle for a one-year deal with the San Francisco Giants, he should be able to find a multi-year deal. He had a stellar defensive season, after defense had been a huge knock on him. He was in contention to win another batting title as well.

Arraez brought a new element to the Phillies offense, and there are not many players like him in baseball. He does not hit for power, but he puts the ball in play, racks up hits and excels at getting on base. It's become a lost art in the modern game, and there is no direct replacement for him in free agency.

However, the Phillies can look at someone else to improve their offense. Just Baseball's Ryan Finkelstein predicted Arraez would ditch Philadelphia for the Kansas City Royals on a four-year, $50 million deal, and that the Phillies would sign Jazz Chisholm Jr. to a two-year, $40 million deal.

Chisholm had a 31-homer, 31-steal season in 2025 and won a Silver Slugger Award. However, he struggled in 2026 and likely cost himself a long-term deal.

"The best case for Jazz is likely a 1+1 deal where he can reset his market and have a pillow of a player option to fall back on," wrote Finkelstein. "The Phillies have too often been in the business of long-term commitments, but this is a case where they can focus on a shorter deal to add a talented, yet unreliable player. There is no doubt that Jazz can add some more thump to the middle of the Phillies lineup. And that would be quite the stage for him to host his second crack at a platform year."

With Arraez and Alec Bohm on the open market, the Phillies have spots in their infield and outfield that could use upgrades. Adding Chisholm would give the Phillies an infield with Bryson Stott at third base, Trea Turner at shortstop, Chisholm at second base and Bryce Harper at first base.

Additionally, the fact that Chisholm could sign on a shorter deal with an out after 2027 could give the Phillies room to sign an outfielder to a long-term deal.

articles.title: Kentucky barely gets votes in new USA TODAY Sports Coaches Poll
articles.summary: Kentucky basketball had a tough week, and are barely clinging to votes in the new USA TODAY Sports Coaches Poll.
articles.body:
Last week was a tough one for Mark Pope and the Kentucky basketball team. They started it by getting blown out by Kansas , then followed that up with a one-point, last second win over Northern Arizona . In both games, they looked lost on both ends of the floor, leading to an unhappy fanbase. It also ended with them falling even further in the USA TODAY Sports Coaches Poll .

They dropped out of the top 25 last week, but this week they barely received any votes at all, getting just two. That would rank them at No. 35, and 9th among teams from the SEC.

The Florida Gators still lead the way for not only the SEC, but the country, holding on to the No. 1 spot again. The Texas Longhorns are also in the top ten, and gained a spot to No. 6. Seven teams are ranked in the top 25, and two more, including Kentucky, received votes.

The Wildcats need wins. They have another big test this week against Indiana on Friday. They have to solve their issues quickly, or risk losing the fans. If they struggle again this week, the calls for Pope's job will get louder, and they won't even get two votes in the poll next week.

articles.title: What Scotland need to secure Nations League promotion play-off spot
articles.summary: Scotland’s victory over North Macedonia keeps their hopes alive of earning promotion
articles.body:
Scotland 's hopes of winning promotion to the top tier of the Nations League are still alive but they will need to pull off a remarkable result when they take on Switzerland tonight.

Sebastien Pocognoli's side were given a boost following their 2-1 victory over North Macedonia on Friday, which ensured they have the chance to overtake Slovenia in the Group B1 table and finish inside the top two.

Switzerland have already sealed automatic promotion to League A as group winners, with the runner-up in B1 advancing to a promotion play-off in March. A third place finish will keep Scotland in the B League, the competition's second tier.

Scotland's fate is out of their hands, so what do Pocognoli's team need in order to secure promotion this evening?

The first and most crucial aspect of Scotland's promotion charge is that they must collect three points when they travel to Switzerland tonight. The Scots head to Sitterstadion in St Gallen with a clear objective but the task will be difficult against a Swiss side who have already secured top spot in the group.

Switzerland top the table with an unassailable 13 points while Slovenia sit second on eight and Scotland are third on seven. Earlier in the group stages, Scotland secured a goalless draw with Slovenia before losing a crucial tie 2-1 at Hampden Park back in early October. That means Slovenia have a superior head-to-head record against Scotland.

Although a draw against Switzerland would be enough to move level on eight points with Slovenia (should they also lose to North Macedonia), Slovenia's superior head-to-head record would win them promotion over Scotland.

All that means Scotland must win this evening and move to 10 points in the table to be in with a chance of getting promoted.

But history is stacked against them. Scotland have met Switzerland five times and have only triumphed once. That victory came in the first meeting between the two nations back in 1996 thanks to an Ally McCoist winner and the Swiss have won two and drawn two of the following four encounters.

Despite that record, optimists may say the Scots are due a win and Switzerland may decide to rest key players with the group already won.

What else must happen if Scotland are to be promoted?

Well, Slovenia have to drop points against North Macedonia. Should Slovenia win their final group game they will finish on 11 points and Scotland will be unable to catch them regardless of the result against the Swiss.

That means a draw between Slovenia and North Macedonia or a North Macedonian victory opens up the route for Scotland to leap ahead of clinch a promotion place.

However, that permutation feels extremely unlikely as North Macedonia haven't earned a single point from their five matches so far. They've been beaten twice by both Switzerland and Scotland and lost 2-0 to Slovenia in their previous contest.

Not only have the North Macedonia's not earned a point yet but they have only scored one goal - in their most recent defeat to the Scots - and that will not trouble a competent and determined Slovenia side.

Yet, should the unlikely scenario occur and North Macedonia take points away from Slovenia at the same time Scotland defeat Switzerland, the Scots will finish second in the group and will be promoted to the top tier of the Nations League

A second place finish would also have a knock-on effect for Euro 2028 as, despite being a co-host, the Tartan Army would be place in an easier qualifying group with a pot two seeding before the draw.

Who could Scotland face in a promotion play-off?

If Scotland manage to finish second in the group, they will advance to the League A/B play-offs in March. They will finish a team from League A who finished either third or fourth in their group.

The permutations for this are slightly confusing: only the two teams with the worst record in League A are automatically relegated, with the two best third-placed teams entering the Nations League finals, along with the League A group winners and runners-up.

The four teams left in the middle will enter the relegation play-offs and face opponents from League B. As it stands, it could be: Wales, Croatia, Serbia, or Norway or Denmark. The draw for the relegation play-offs will be made on Friday. The matches will take place over two legs in March.
